Addon_Beartrap_001.name: Honing Stone
Addon_Beartrap_001.description:
When used with the Bear Trap, the honing stone sharpens its blades. The razor-sharp blades inflicts deep wounds aimed at bleeding the victim as fast as possible.

The trapped victim is left dying instead of injured if they free themselves.

beginner.whatItIs: Attaches to Bear Trap and sharpens the blades so that any survivor who frees themselves drops into the dying state instead of the injured one. A successful escape becomes a death race rather than a manageable injury.
beginner.whyItMatters: Turning an escape into a dying state is a major shift in how the trap functions, since a dying survivor has almost no margin before becoming a hook target. It forces the team to divert attention at exactly the moment they thought the threat was over.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in lobbies where survivors are confident in their trap-disarming speed, because it punishes the exact moment they think they are safe. It is a very rare drop and will not appear often in your collection.

Addon_Beartrap_002.name: Serrated Jaws
Addon_Beartrap_002.description:
These replacement Bear Trap jaws have saw like blades which cause awful open wounds when they snap.

Bear Traps inflict Hemorrhage on trapped Survivors until they are healed.

Hemorrhage regresses healing progress when not healing, and increases blood trails left by injured Survivors. This lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Replaces the standard jaws inside Bear Trap with saw-toothed blades that inflict Hemorrhage on any survivor caught in the trap. The bleeding condition erodes healing progress over time and leaves a more pronounced blood trail behind the injured survivor.
beginner.whyItMatters: Adding a bleeding condition on top of the standard injury makes it harder for the caught survivor to finish a heal and easier for The Trapper to track them afterward. It changes the escape from a clean break into a lingering problem that follows the survivor through the rest of the trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team relies heavily on healing after escapes, because the bleeding penalty makes quick patches much harder to complete. The drop rate is uncommon, so the locker should see it with fair regularity over a reasonable number of trials.

Addon_Beartrap_003.name: Trapper Bag
Addon_Beartrap_003.description:
A cured leather waist bag. Large and sturdy to transport hunting equipment.

Start with 1 extra Bear Trap.Allows the transportation of 1 extra Bear Trap.

beginner.whatItIs: Trapper Bag adds an extra Bear Trap to the loadout The Trapper carries at the start of the trial. That additional unit can be placed early, widening the zone under killer control before survivors finish their first rotation.
beginner.whyItMatters: An extra trap on the map from the opening seconds gives The Trapper more leeway to control multiple corridors at once without burning time walking back for a placement. It reads as a meaningful improvement rather than a small tweak, since it effectively adds another controlled tile to the opening setup.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when you want a denser trap field early in the trial, especially on maps with multiple generator loops that survivors will travel between. It is a rare drop, so it will not be in your inventory on every match.

Addon_Beartrap_004.name: Wax Brick
Addon_Beartrap_004.description:
A block of wax used to lower friction and facilitate movement in mechanical parts.

Increases the time required to rescue a Survivor or attempt escape from a Bear Trap by 33%.

beginner.whatItIs: Coats the mechanism inside Bear Trap and slows down the process of freeing a trapped survivor, whether a teammate attempts a rescue or the trapped survivor works to escape alone. The added friction makes both actions take noticeably longer than normal.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer lock-in window gives The Trapper more time to reach the trap site and turn a quick save into a chase or a hook. It protects the trap investment by making the rescue window feel tighter for the team, which discourages early saves.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the lobby has strong rescuers who would otherwise pull teammates out before you can react. It is an uncommon rarity, so expect it to land in your inventory on a fairly steady basis.

Addon_Beartrap_005.name: Lengthened Jaws
Addon_Beartrap_005.description:
Jaws with long teeth that dig further into the flesh than a conventional Bear Trap.

When Survivors escape Bear Traps, they are inflicted with Deep Wound.

Deep Wound will put a Survivor in the dying state unless it is mended before the timer runs out.

beginner.whatItIs: Swaps the trap teeth for longer, deeper-jawed blades that inflict Deep Wound when a survivor escapes Bear Trap. If the wound is not mended before its timer expires, the injured survivor drops into the dying state.
beginner.whyItMatters: Adding a countdown to every escape forces the caught survivor to choose between healing immediately or risking death, which splits team focus at a critical moment. It turns a standard escape into a pressure point that the whole group feels.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when you want to keep pressure on a survivor after they break free, rather than relying solely on the trap's initial hit. It is an uncommon drop, so it should be reasonably available in your locker.

Addon_Beartrap_006.name: Tar Bottle
Addon_Beartrap_006.description:
A black, matte and sticky substance similar to tar. When applied to Bear Traps, makes them far less noticeable.

Darkens the appearance of Bear Traps.

beginner.whatItIs: Darkens the appearance of Bear Trap with a matte, sticky coating that helps the traps blend into the environment. The visual change makes it harder for survivors to spot a placed trap at a glance.
beginner.whyItMatters: A trap that is easy to overlook can catch a survivor who walks straight through it, turning a well-traveled tile into a silent hazard with no audible warning. The surprise factor matters most in tight maps where survivors assume they know every safe path.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when you want to rely on ambush rather than speed, since hidden traps punish survivors who are not paying close attention to the ground. It is a rare drop, so expect to wait a few trials before it appears.

Addon_Beartrap_007.name: Makeshift Wrap
Addon_Beartrap_007.description:
A scratched and worn brace made of thick, cured animal skin.

The Trapper cannot be caught in his Bear Traps.Bear Traps will be disarmed if The Trapper steps on them.

beginner.whatItIs: Makeshift Wrap protects The Trapper from being caught in his own Bear Traps while walking through his trap lines. If he does step on one, the trap disarms itself harmlessly instead of triggering.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the self-catch risk means The Trapper can walk freely through his own trap lines while adjusting positions or pursuing a survivor. It makes dense cluster setups around generators and loops much safer to maintain throughout the trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in early trials to build confidence, since it removes one of the most frustrating mistakes a new Trapper player can make. It is a common rarity, so it should be easy to find in your locker.

Addon_Beartrap_008.name: 4-Coil Spring Kit
Addon_Beartrap_008.description:
A replacement kit for Bear Traps which changes the usual dual spring system with 4 coil springs adding a great amount of strength to the traps' hold.

Increases time required for Survivors to disarm Bear Traps by 33%.

beginner.whatItIs: Reinforces the spring system inside Bear Trap, making it take noticeably longer for a survivor to disarm the catch. The stronger hold resists the quick-release motion that survivors rely on to escape.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stretches how long a survivor struggles with the blade before the trap releases, buying The Trapper enough room to close the gap or position a second trap nearby. The shift lands as a meaningful nudge rather than a full redesign, keeping the Bear Trap core loop intact while tightening the escape window around it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when survivors are disarming traps too quickly and the chase starts before The Trapper can arrive at the scene. The drop rate is uncommon, so expect it to appear in the locker with reasonable consistency over time.

Addon_Beartrap_009.name: Trapper Sack
Addon_Beartrap_009.description:
A crude leather sack suitable for foraging.

All Bear Traps are carried at the beginning of the Trial instead of spawning on the map.Bear Traps cannot be picked up.

beginner.whatItIs: Changes how Bear Trap deploys by making The Trapper carry every trap from the start of the trial. Once a trap is placed on the ground it cannot be picked up again, so each spot becomes a permanent commitment.
beginner.whyItMatters: Locking every trap position early in the trial is a significant shift in pacing, since each placement must be deliberate and cannot be repositioned if survivor routes change. It rewards a killer who plans their map control before the first generator progress happens.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when you want to play a committed map-control style where the trap layout is fixed before the survivors start moving. It is a very rare drop, so expect to wait a long time before it lands in your locker.

Addon_Beartrap_010.name: Trapper Gloves
Addon_Beartrap_010.description:
Protective padded leather gloves.

Increases Bear Trap setting speed by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Speeds up the placement animation for Bear Trap, letting The Trapper set each trap faster than the standard pace. The reduced set time shrinks the vulnerable window where The Trapper stands still with the trap raised.
beginner.whyItMatters: A quicker placement means less time spent frozen in the set animation, which shrinks the window a survivor has to spot and avoid the trap going down. It is a small but reliable improvement that compounds over every trap laid in a trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it whenever setting up a trap line in a hurry, especially when moving between adjacent spots and needing to minimize the time spent in the placement animation. The rarity is common, so the locker should have several copies available at all times.

Addon_Beartrap_011.name: Secondary Coil
Addon_Beartrap_011.description:
A secondary coil which keeps a Bear Trap effective in times when the primary coils becomes unusable.

Increases time required for Survivors to disarm Bear Traps by 50%.

beginner.whatItIs: An add-on for Bear Trap that adds a secondary spring to slow down the disarming process. Survivors who find a trapped coil still in the ground need noticeably more time to cut it free.
beginner.whyItMatters: A trapped survivor sits immobilized far longer, which gives The Trapper a wide window to close the distance and hook them before help arrives. It reads as a meaningful shift in how each trap converts into progress rather than a minor nudge.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a single well-placed trap needs to hold a survivor long enough for you to walk the full distance to them. Its rarity is rare, so the drop may take several trials to land in your pool.

Addon_Beartrap_012.name: Fastening Tools
Addon_Beartrap_012.description:
A specialized set of tools used to fasten Bear Traps to ensure their effectiveness.

Increases Bear Trap setting speed by 50%.Increases the time required to rescue a Survivor or attempt escape from a Bear Trap by 25%.

beginner.whatItIs: Fastening Tools speeds up the placement of Bear Trap and also stretches the time a trapped survivor takes to free themselves. The result is a trap that appears faster and holds longer once it snaps shut.
beginner.whyItMatters: Quicker placement rewards aggressive movement between traps, while the extended lock-in means each catch converts into a hook more reliably. Together the two effects push Bear Trap from a reactive tool toward a more proactive tempo.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when The Trapper needs to cover a lot of ground between trap placements and wants each one to stick long enough for rescue attempts to fail. Because it is a rare find, plan around having it ready rather than assuming it will appear in every match.

Addon_Beartrap_PaddedJaws.name: Padded Jaws
Addon_Beartrap_PaddedJaws.description:
These padded jaws are meant to restrain, not to wound.

Bear Traps do not inflict damage on trapped Survivors. Equipping this add-on negates the effects of Rusted Jaws and Serrated Jaws.Points awarded for trapping Survivors are increased by 100%.

beginner.whatItIs: Padded Jaws slots into Bear Trap and removes all damage from the jaws, so a caught survivor takes no injury at all. It also cancels the effects of Rusted Jaws and Serrated Jaws if those were otherwise equipped.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stripping away the damage reshapes the trap into a pure holding mechanism, shifting the killer's focus from punishing escapes toward positioning and score. That is a larger conceptual shift than most trap add-ons, since it changes what the trap actually does to the survivor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you play a score-chasing or positional style of Trapper and do not want the trap to hurt the survivor on contact. It is a common rarity, so expect to find it without much effort.

Addon_Beartrap_TrapperSack.name: Bear Oil
Addon_Beartrap_TrapperSack.description:
Melted animal fat that can lubricate the Bear Trap's squeaky joints.

Setting a Bear Trap is silent.

beginner.whatItIs: Bear Oil coats the joints of Bear Trap with melted fat so that the act of placing it produces no audible sound. Survivors in earshot cannot pick up the mechanical clink that would otherwise give the tile away.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the placement sound takes away one of the main audio cues survivors use to avoid stepping on a coil. A trap set in silence can sit right next to a survivor's path without warning them at all.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when setting a trap close enough to a survivor that the normal clicking would tip them off, or when you want to lay one behind them mid-chase without alerting them. Since it is common, the drop will arrive without much waiting.

Addon_Bell_001.name: Bone Clapper
Addon_Bell_001.description: A bell clapper made from a highly polished piece of bone. Causes the sounds of the Wailing Bell to echo and warp chaotically.Survivors can no longer discern the Wailing Bell's distance or direction.

beginner.whatItIs: Bone Clapper replaces the Wailing Bell's clapper with one made of polished bone, warping the echo until it scatters in unpredictable directions. Survivors can no longer judge either the distance or the bearing of the sound.
beginner.whyItMatters: Without reliable distance or bearing information, survivors lose their primary audio tool for locating the Wraith during the cloak phase. That forces them to guess or rely on other cues, wasting time and sending them down the wrong corridor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it whenever The Wraith wants to mask the bell true bearing so survivors chase phantom echoes across the map, turning their map pings into dead ends. It appears at an uncommon drop rate, so expect it to show up regularly in the offering pool during a session.

Addon_Bell_002.name: "The Ghost" - Soot
Addon_Bell_002.description:
The Khugwemuu symbol, representing the spirit world, is finger-drawn out of soot on the body of the bell.

After Uncloaking, the Wraith's Terror Radius and Red Stain will remain suppressed for 6 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: "The Ghost" is a soot-drawn symbol on the Wailing Bell that keeps the Wraith's Terror Radius and Red Stain invisible for a short window after uncloaking. Survivors get no aura highlight and no red glow to signal the killer's arrival.
beginner.whyItMatters: Hiding the Terror Radius and Red Stain for that brief post-uncloak window lets the Wraith step into close range before any survivor notices a change on their screen. It turns the moment of appearance into an unannounced arrival, which sets up the opening attack with far less warning.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when you want the uncloak to catch survivors completely flat, since they have zero visual warning that the Wraith is already beside them. It is a common drop, so the symbol should appear in the locker without too much patience.

Addon_Bell_003.name: "The Hound" - Soot
Addon_Bell_003.description:
The Wonnug symbol, representing a peerless tracker, is finger-drawn out of soot on the body of the bell.

While Cloaked, fresh blood marks are brighter than normal.

beginner.whatItIs: "The Hound" is a soot-drawn tracker symbol on the Wailing Bell that makes fresh blood marks glow brighter than usual while the Wraith remains cloaked. The effect only runs during the hidden phase and fades the moment the Wraith reveals itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: A brighter trail during the cloak phase lets the Wraith read recent survivor paths at a glance and pick a chase target with less guesswork. It trims wasted movement before the first attack and makes the opening encounter feel more deliberate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when choosing which survivor to hunt feels uncertain, because the heightened blood marks make the most recently active route stand out clearly. The common rarity means it lands in the pool without needing many trials to find.

Addon_Bell_004.name: "Blind Warrior" - Mud
Addon_Bell_004.description:
The Baikra-Kaeug symbol, representing ferocity, is finger-drawn in mud on the body of the Bell.

Uncloak surprise attacks inflict Survivors with Blindness for 60 seconds. Blindness prevents survivors from seeing auras.

beginner.whatItIs: "Blind Warrior" is a mud-drawn ferocity symbol on the Wailing Bell that blinds the target of a surprise attack after uncloaking. A blinded survivor loses the ability to see any auras for an extended stretch.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing aura vision from the target means they cannot tell which teammates are injured or where the killer currently stands. That opens the door to chaotic chases and makes coordinated rescues far harder for the rest of the team.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the opening attack after uncloaking should ripple through the whole survivor team, scrambling their ability to track each other. The uncommon rate of appearance means it will not be in every locker, but it does land with reasonable regularity.

Addon_Bell_005.name: "Swift Hunt" - Mud
Addon_Bell_005.description:
The Kuntin-Takkho symbol, representing rapid descent on prey, is finger-drawn in mud on the body of the Bell.

Increases uncloaking speed by 8%.

beginner.whatItIs: A Wailing Bell add-on that speeds up how quickly The Wraith emerges from cloaking. The Kuntin-Takkho symbol finger-drawn in mud on the bell body is what grants the effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: Uncloaking faster means The Wraith can drop onto a survivor and land the first swing before they can react, which is where a bell hunt is often won or lost. It reads as a small but tangible edge rather than a full change to how the power works.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you already know how to cloak behind a survivor and want the transition to the strike to feel snappier. It is an uncommon drop and will show up often enough to build around without much effort.

Addon_Bell_006.name: "Swift Hunt" - Blood
Addon_Bell_006.description:
The Kuntin-Takkho symbol, representing rapid descent on prey, is stamped in blood on the head of the Bell.

Increases uncloaking speed by 12%.

beginner.whatItIs: The blood-stamped Kuntin-Takkho symbol on a Wailing Bell pushes uncloaking speed higher than the mud variant. The stamp sits on the head of the bell, which is where the stronger effect lives.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra uncloak speed closes the gap between the moment a survivor looks up and the moment The Wraith is fully there, which matters most in close-range bell fights where timing is everything. It is a meaningful upgrade over the mud version without changing the core loop of hiding and dropping.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Save this for a dedicated bell build where you already hide behind survivors regularly and want the drop to feel more decisive. It is a very rare add-on and worth keeping for a focused Wraith loadout.

Addon_Bell_007.name: "The Beast" - Soot
Addon_Bell_007.description:
The Kunwulju symbol, representing the realm of fear, is finger-drawn out of soot on the body of the bell.

The Wraith's Terror Radius is no longer suppressed while Cloaked.Bloodpoints granted for Stalking and surprise attacks are increased by 100%.

beginner.whatItIs: A Wailing Bell add-on that keeps The Wraith's Terror Radius active even while cloaked and also doubles the Bloodpoints earned from Stalking and surprise attacks. The Kunwulju symbol drawn in soot on the bell body ties both effects together.
beginner.whyItMatters: Survivors inside a Terror Radius hear the killer's breathing, so keeping it on while cloaked removes the one safe window they normally use to slip past The Wraith. The Bloodpoint bonus on top makes this a bigger shift in how the bell feels to play rather than a small speed tweak.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when you want to punish survivors who try to walk past The Wraith while it is hidden, since the exposed Terror Radius makes that risky for them. It is a common drop and easy to slot in for testing without hunting for anything rarer.

Addon_Bell_008.name: "All Seeing" - Blood
Addon_Bell_008.description:
The Kra-Frabai symbol, representing The Entity watching over us, is stamped in blood on the head of the Bell.

Unlocks hidden potential in one's aura reading ability. While Cloaked, the auras of Survivors within 8 meters are revealed to you.

beginner.whatItIs: A Wailing Bell add-on that reveals the auras of nearby survivors while The Wraith is cloaked. The Kra-Frabai symbol stamped on the head of the bell represents The Entity watching, which fits the sight-granting effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: Seeing where survivors are while still hidden lets The Wraith pick its next target or reposition without giving up the cloak, which is a meaningful advantage in a power that is all about staying unseen. It is a bigger shift than a speed tweak because it adds information that the base power does not provide.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a chase has gone quiet and you need to confirm whether survivors are still nearby before committing to another bell strike. Since it drops very rarely, hold it for a Wailing Bell loadout that already prioritizes staying cloaked while reading the map.

Addon_Bell_009.name: "Windstorm"- Mud
Addon_Bell_009.description: The Ohuwe-Onmnea symbol, representing a howling storm, is finger-drawn in mud on the body of the Bell.Increases the Wraith's movement speed while cloaked by 5%.

beginner.whatItIs: An Ohuwe-Onmnea symbol drawn in mud on a Wailing Bell that makes The Wraith move slightly faster while cloaked. The symbol represents a howling storm, which matches the speed boost.
beginner.whyItMatters: Moving faster while cloaked lets The Wraith reposition between survivors or track a target without breaking the cloak, which keeps the pressure on without revealing The Wraith's position. It is a small but steady improvement to the bell's core loop of hiding and hunting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when you want to chase survivors from a hidden state and need to close distance quickly without uncloaking. It is an uncommon drop and pairs well with other cloak-focused add-ons on a Wraith build.

Addon_Bell_010.name: "Windstorm" - White
Addon_Bell_010.description: The Ohuwe-Onmnea symbol, representing a howling storm, is finger-drawn in white ink on the body of the Bell.Increases the Wraith's movement speed while cloaked by 7%.

beginner.whatItIs: The Ohuwe-Onmnea symbol drawn in white ink on a Wailing Bell, pushing The Wraith's cloaked movement speed higher than the mud version. The white ink on the bell body is what carries the stronger boost.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra speed while cloaked lets The Wraith keep pace with a sprinting survivor from behind without breaking the cloak, which is the whole point of a bell build. It reads as a meaningful upgrade over the mud variant because the speed difference is felt in every chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Save this for a Wraith build that already leans on tracking survivors from a hidden state, since the extra speed makes that style more punishing. It is a rare drop and worth keeping for a dedicated bell loadout.

Addon_Bell_011.name: "Blink" - Mud
Addon_Bell_011.description:
The Kratin symbol, representing quick passing, is finger-drawn in mud on the body of the Bell.

Increases cloaking speed by 40%.

beginner.whatItIs: An uncommon Wailing Bell add-on stamped with the Kratin symbol, hand-drawn in mud to represent quick passing. It makes The Wraith slide into cloaking noticeably faster than the base animation allows.
beginner.whyItMatters: Cloaking faster means The Wraith vanishes from a survivor's view before they can react or loop, which is where the bell power does most of its damage. It is a bigger shift than the movement speed add-ons because it changes how quickly The Wraith can disappear, not just how fast it moves while hidden.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slip it into a Wailing Bell loadout whenever The Wraith needs to drop out of sight the moment a survivor notices the chase. The faster cloak makes it easier to punish a survivor who pauses to loot a chest or break a pallet during the chase.

Addon_Bell_012.name: "Blink" - White
Addon_Bell_012.description:
The Kratin symbol, representing quick passing, is finger-drawn in white ink on the body of the Bell.

Increases cloaking speed by 60%.

beginner.whatItIs: Stamped in white ink across a Wailing Bell, the Kratin symbol here represents quick passing and pushes The Wraith's cloaking speed past the level the mud version reaches. It is a rare drop that slots into the same power as the lesser ink variant.
beginner.whyItMatters: The Wraith drops out of sight so quickly that survivors rarely get the beat they need to start looping or call for backup. This changes the tempo of every chase because The Wraith can reposition and re-cloak before a survivor has time to react.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Reach for it when a Wailing Bell loadout already focuses on vanishing mid-chase and The Wraith needs the cloak to close before a survivor can break a pallet. Its rare drop rate suits a dedicated bell build more than a mixed one.

ADDON_Bell_AllseeingSpirit.name: "All Seeing" - Spirit
ADDON_Bell_AllseeingSpirit.description:
The Kra-Frabai symbol, representing The Entity watching over us, glows ominously on the head of the bell.

Unlocks awesome potential in one's aura reading ability. While Cloaked, the repair progress of generators can be determined by the intensity of their auras.

beginner.whatItIs: An add-on for the Wailing Bell that lets the killer gauge how far survivors have progressed on generators while cloaked. It shows that repair progress through the intensity of each generator's aura.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reading progress from a distance means the killer can pick which generator to strike without breaking the cloak first. That turns the hidden state into a scouting tool that loses nothing, so it reads as a bigger shift than a small tweak.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on iridescent rolls if the playstyle leans on silent scouting. It is most useful when stalking between generators and deciding the next move from a distance.

ADDON_Bell_AllseeingWhite.name: "The Serpent" - Soot
ADDON_Bell_AllseeingWhite.description:
The Oas-Nek symbol, representing cunning, is finger-drawn out of soot on the body of the bell.

While Cloaked, uncloak whenever you basic-break Pallets or Breakable Walls, and damage or explode Generators.

beginner.whatItIs: A Wailing Bell add-on that forces the cloak to drop whenever the killer basic-breaks pallets or breakable walls, or damages or explodes generators. The trade is that those actions no longer keep the killer hidden.
beginner.whyItMatters: Those utility actions now cost stealth, so the killer must choose between staying unseen and getting the faster break. That is a bigger shift in how the power plays, not a small number tweak.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on common rolls if escaping a chase matters more than staying hidden. It helps when the killer wants quick pallet breaks and wall drops as an escape route.

ADDON_Bell_BlindBlood.name: "Shadow Dance" - White
ADDON_Bell_BlindBlood.description:
The Yiwarick symbol, representing dark synergy, is finger-drawn in white ink on the body of the Bell.

While Cloaked, you basic-vault Windows, basic-break Pallets and Breakable Walls, and damage Generators 40% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A Wailing Bell add-on that lets the cloaked killer basic-vault windows, break pallets and breakable walls, and damage generators at an improved pace. Every one of those actions keeps the cloak up while it happens.
beginner.whyItMatters: The cloaked state becomes far more mobile, since the killer can chase and clear obstacles without giving up its hiding. That is a bigger change to the power's rhythm than a small tweak.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on rare rolls when a chase-heavy approach feels right. It shines when the killer wants to stay unseen through a full pursuit while still crossing windows and breaking pallets quickly.

ADDON_Bell_BlindSpirit.name: "Shadow Dance" - Blood
ADDON_Bell_BlindSpirit.description:
The Yiwarick symbol, representing dark synergy, is stamped in blood on the body of the Bell.

While Cloaked, you basic-vault Windows, basic-break Pallets and Breakable Walls, and damage Generators 60% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A Wailing Bell add-on in the Shadow Dance line that pushes cloaked vaulting, pallet breaking, wall breaking and generator damage even further than its white-ink sibling. It keeps the cloak up through all of those actions.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra speed makes the cloaked state feel like a second chase mode, since the killer can move through windows and clear pallets in a hurry while staying hidden. That is a meaningful change to the power's flow.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Grab it on very rare rolls if chases feel slow to set up without it. Good for a killer who wants the cloaked state to carry a whole pursuit, not just a single vault.

ADDON_Bell_BlindWhite.name: "Blind Warrior" - White
ADDON_Bell_BlindWhite.description:
The Baikra-Kaeug symbol, representing ferocity, is finger-drawn in white ink on the body of the Bell.

Uncloak surprise attacks inflict Mangled and Hemorrhage for 70 seconds.

Hemorrhage regresses healing progress when not healing, and increases blood trails left by injured survivors. This lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

Mangled increases time required to heal by 25% and lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Marks survivors hit by an uncloak surprise attack with Mangled and Hemorrhage, both of which slow healing. Hemorrhage also thickens the blood trail while the survivor is not healing.
beginner.whyItMatters: The aftermath of a single surprise hit now weighs on the survivor during healing, which adds real follow-up pressure. That is a bigger shift than a small speed tweak, because the punishment lands after the escape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on rare rolls when the killer relies on ambushes to open hunts. It pays off whenever an uncloak strike lands, since the survivor keeps feeling it while trying to mend.

ADDON_Bell_CoxcombedClapper.name: Coxcombed Clapper
ADDON_Bell_CoxcombedClapper.description:
A simple coxcomb knotted rope wrapped around the bell clapper to muffle its sound. A malevolent aura emanates from it.

Renders the Wailing Bell completely silent.

beginner.whatItIs: It ties a knotted rope around the clapper of the Wailing Bell, muting the ring entirely. The power still triggers and affects survivors, but the bell makes no noise when it sounds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the sound takes away an auditory cue that survivors can react to, so the bell's effect lands with no warning. That is a meaningful change for a stealth-focused build rather than a small number nudge.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Save it for iridescent rolls where silence is the whole point of the build. It fits best on a Wailing Bell setup that already tries to stay hidden, since the payoff is the absence of noise.

ADDON_Bell_SwiftMud.name: "Swift Hunt" - White
ADDON_Bell_SwiftMud.description:
The Kuntin-Takkho symbol, representing rapid descent on prey, is finger-drawn in white ink on the body of the Bell.

Increases uncloaking speed by 10%.

beginner.whatItIs: Raises the speed at which the Wailing Bell drops its cloak, making the uncloak transition quicker. The killer emerges from the hidden state in a shorter window.
beginner.whyItMatters: A faster uncloak shortens the vulnerable gap between hidden and visible, which matters most in the instant before an attack. It reads as a small but dependable tweak to the power's timing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on rare rolls if the uncloak window feels too slow to trust. It helps on chases where the killer needs to come out of the cloak and swing in a hurry.

ADDON_Bell_WindstormBlood.name: "Windstorm" - Blood
ADDON_Bell_WindstormBlood.description:
The Ohuwe-Onmnea symbol, representing a howling storm, is stamped in blood on the body of the bell.

Increases the Wraith's movement speed while cloaked by 9%.

beginner.whatItIs: Speeds up the Wraith's movement while cloaked, making the hidden state quicker to move in. The Wraith covers more ground in the same amount of hidden time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster hidden movement lets the killer scout and reposition between threats with less exposure. That is a meaningful boost to the cloaked role rather than a small number nudge.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Grab it on very rare rolls when the build leans on scouting from a distance. It suits the killer who wants to cross a map's length while staying out of sight.

Addon_Blinker_001.name: Plaid Flannel
Addon_Blinker_001.description:
A torn piece of red and black plaid flannel. The scrap of fabric imbues The Nurse with devastating focus.

Allows the Nurse to see the Blink target location.

beginner.whatItIs: Plaid Flannel slots into Spencer's Last Breath and reveals the target location of a Blink to The Nurse. Without it, the landing spot for a Blink Attack is invisible until the lunge actually happens.
beginner.whyItMatters: Seeing where a Blink will land before committing to it removes a lot of the guesswork from the power, since The Nurse can now line up a clean hit on a survivor in a loop or on a generator. It reads as a bigger shift in how the power plays because it turns a blind lunge into an aimed one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it to stop missing Blink Attacks by accident, since it gives a clearer picture of where the lunge will connect. It is a common drop and a good first add-on to slot into a Nurse build.

Addon_Blinker_002.name: White Nit Comb
Addon_Blinker_002.description:
A parasitic nit comb taken from the clinic. Once the symbol of a deep connection between an anxious patient and her nurse.

Decreases the length of Blink Attack lunges by 50%.Increases Bloodpoints for Blink Attack score events by 100%.

beginner.whatItIs: White Nit Comb slots into Spencer's Last Breath and shortens the lunge distance of Blink Attacks while doubling the Bloodpoints earned from scoring with them. The shorter lunge makes each hit feel more controlled and less like a gamble.
beginner.whyItMatters: A shorter lunge means The Nurse is less likely to overshoot a survivor or get caught on a pallet, which makes the power feel more reliable in tight chases. The Bloodpoint bonus on top rewards clean hits and makes the power more satisfying to play.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when Blink Attacks feel too long and unpredictable, since the shorter lunge makes each hit easier to land. It is a common drop and pairs well with a precision-focused Nurse build.

Addon_Blinker_003.name: Pocket Watch
Addon_Blinker_003.description:
A charred and broken pocket watch with rattling pieces. Taken from Nurse Moris' body.

Increases the time before The Nurse succumbs to fatigue after Blinking by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Pocket Watch slots into Spencer's Last Breath and buys The Nurse more time before fatigue sets in after each Blink. The charred, rattling watch is a relic from Nurse Moris and carries the time-extension effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: More time before fatigue means The Nurse can string together more Blinks in a single chase without being forced to stop, which is exactly what a Nurse build is built around. It reads as a small but steady improvement that makes every chase feel slightly more sustainable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when you want to chase longer without being cut off by fatigue after the first Blink. It is an uncommon drop and a solid addition to any Nurse build that already leans on chaining Blinks.

Addon_Blinker_004.name: Anxious Gasp
Addon_Blinker_004.description:
The gasp of surprise collected from an anxious girl which The Nurse was fond of. Twitches vigorously at The Nurse's touch.

Blinking past a survivor causes them to scream and awards 200 Bloodpoints for spooking them.

beginner.whatItIs: Anxious Gasp is a rare add-on for Spencer's Last Breath that makes survivors scream when The Nurse Blinks past them, while also awarding a chunk of Bloodpoints for the spook. The gasp was collected from an anxious patient and twitches at The Nurse's touch.
beginner.whyItMatters: The scream gives away a survivor's position to the rest of the team, which can pull other survivors into a dangerous spot or break a quiet generator run. The Bloodpoint bonus on top makes it a small reward for taking the risk of Blinking past someone who might not even be looking.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Add it to a Spencer's Last Breath build whenever you want a clean Blink to leave an audio trail that other survivors can hear. The scream it triggers can drag a hiding survivor out from behind a pallet or near a generator, and the rare drop rate makes it worth holding for a Nurse loadout that thrives on chaos.

Addon_Blinker_005.name: Torn Bookmark
Addon_Blinker_005.description:
A white and pristine piece of ribbon once attached to a sacred book. Serves as the symbol of a dispute.

Adds 1 Blink charge.Increases Blink recharge time by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Torn Bookmark is an iridescent ribbon once attached to a sacred book that slots into Spencer's Last Breath and adds an extra Blink charge at the cost of slower recharge. The extra charge is a meaningful trade-off, since the recharge penalty slows the whole power down.
beginner.whyItMatters: Having an extra charge ready means The Nurse can Blink twice in quick succession during a chase, which is a genuine shift in how the power plays compared to the base setup. The slower recharge is the price, so the power feels more bursty and less sustained.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if you want to land two Blinks back to back in a single chase and can live with the slower recharge between them. It is an iridescent drop and worth saving for a Nurse build that already chains Blinks well.

Addon_Blinker_006.name: Dark Cincture
Addon_Blinker_006.description:
A black rope used as a belt in times of mourning. Taken from Father Campbell's body.

Increases movement speed after a Blink but before the following fatigue by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Dark Cincture is a black mourning rope that slots into Spencer's Last Breath and boosts The Nurse's movement speed for a short window after each Blink, before fatigue kicks in. It was taken from Father Campbell's body.
beginner.whyItMatters: The speed burst after a Blink lets The Nurse close the gap to a survivor or escape a bad reposition before fatigue slows them down, which is exactly the moment where a Nurse chase is won or lost. It is a small but timely boost that makes each Blink feel more rewarding.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when you want to follow up a Blink with a strong push toward a survivor before fatigue sets in. It is an uncommon drop and fits naturally into a Nurse build that already commits to Blinks often.

Addon_Blinker_007.name: Fragile Wheeze
Addon_Blinker_007.description:
The whistling and rattling breath stolen from Father Campbell. Silently curves and bends at The Nurse's touch.

Blink Attacks inflict the Mangled status effect for 70 seconds.

Mangled increases time required to heal by 25% and lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Fragile Wheeze slots into Spencer's Last Breath and makes every successful Blink Attack leave the Mangled status on the hit survivor, slowing their healing progress for a set window. The rattling breath was originally stolen from Father Campbell.
beginner.whyItMatters: Slowing healing after a hit means a survivor who takes a Blink Attack needs longer at a generator to recover, which gives The Nurse more time to loop back and press the advantage. It is a meaningful shift in chase dynamics because it extends the punishment of a clean hit well beyond the moment it lands.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a Nurse build already lands clean Blink hits and you want each one to extend the pain into the next heal attempt. The Mangled effect stretches recovery time just enough to deny a survivor the comfort of a quick top-up, and its rare drop rate makes it a keep-and-forget addition to a dedicated loadout.

Addon_Blinker_008.name: Campbell's Last Breath
Addon_Blinker_008.description:
A powerful last breath snatched from Crotus Prenn asylum priest Father Campbell. In the hands of The Nurse, it crackles with intensity.

After reappearing from a fully charged Blink, The Nurse immediately Blinks at full charge in the direction she is currently facing.This only works if The Nurse has a remaining Blink charge.

beginner.whatItIs: Snatched from Father Campbell's cold grip, Campbell's Last Breath lets The Nurse fire a second full-charge Blink the instant she reappears from the first, aimed in whatever direction she is facing. The Breath slots into Spencer's Last Breath and only triggers when a spare charge is available.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaining two full Blinks in a row is a big shift in how the power plays, since it lets The Nurse cover far more ground in a single chase without waiting for a recharge. It turns a single lunge into a double lunge, which can carry a survivor across a large part of the map in one move.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Reach for it when a single chase needs The Nurse to cross a long open field in one burst and disappear at the far end before survivors can react. Its very rare drop rate suits a dedicated Spencer's Last Breath loadout that already commits to full-charge Blinks as the main tool.

Addon_Blinker_009.name: Metal Spoon
Addon_Blinker_009.description:
A dull, partially rusted and stained metallic spoon. Confiscated from room 202's patient, the "Bad Man".

Hitting a survivor with a successful Blink Attack causes their sounds of pain to be 50% louder for 60 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Metal Spoon is a dull, rusted spoon confiscated from a patient in the asylum that slots into Spencer's Last Breath and makes a survivor's pain sounds louder after a successful Blink Attack. The louder noise gives away the survivor's position more clearly.
beginner.whyItMatters: A clean Blink hit becomes an audio beacon that every nearby survivor can track, exposing where the struck survivor is to anyone within earshot. This small information edge rewards The Nurse for landing precise hits and can collapse a quiet generator phase into a chaotic scramble.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when you want to keep pressure on a survivor who just got hit, since the louder noise makes it harder for them to stay hidden. It is a common drop that adds a useful tracking layer to a Nurse build.

Addon_Blinker_010.name: Bad Man Keepsake
Addon_Blinker_010.description:
A rotten molar extirpated from the "Bad Man's" cold dead hand.

Hitting a survivor with a successful Blink Attack causes their aura to be revealed when healing or being healed within a 28 meter range for 60 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Bad Man Keepsake is a rotten molar taken from a patient's cold dead hand that slots into Spencer's Last Breath and reveals a survivor's aura while they are healing or being healed after a successful Blink Attack. The reveal lasts for a set window after the hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Seeing a survivor's aura while they heal means The Nurse can loop back and interrupt them, which turns a clean hit into a much bigger advantage. It is a meaningful information tool because it extends the value of a Blink Attack well beyond the moment it lands.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a Nurse build wants every clean Blink to leave a trail that follows the survivor into their next heal. The aura reveal turns a healing session into a risk for the whole team, and its uncommon rate means it is easy to work into any Spencer's Last Breath loadout.

Addon_Blinker_011.name: Wooden Horse
Addon_Blinker_011.description:
An unpainted toy carved out of cheap wood to resemble a horse. Once the symbol of a deep connection between a catatonic patient and his nurse.

Decreases extra fatigue from missed Blink Attacks by 50%.

beginner.whatItIs: Wooden Horse is an unpainted toy horse carved from cheap wood that slots into Spencer's Last Breath and cuts the extra fatigue The Nurse suffers from missed Blink Attacks by a large margin. It was once a comfort object for a catatonic patient.
beginner.whyItMatters: Missing a Blink Attack normally punishes The Nurse with extra fatigue, which can end a chase before it even gets going. Cutting that penalty means The Nurse can take riskier Blinks without being as heavily punished for a miss, which makes the power feel more forgiving.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when you want to commit to Blinks more freely without being as scared of a miss, since the reduced fatigue penalty makes each attempt feel safer. It is a common drop that suits an aggressive Nurse build well.

Addon_Blinker_012.name: Catatonic Boy's Treasure
Addon_Blinker_012.description:
A pine-cone which unexpectedly calmed a patient's repetitive movement. Taken from the catatonic boy's body.

Decreases extra fatigue from chain Blinks by 65%.

beginner.whatItIs: Catatonic Boy's Treasure is a pine-cone that once calmed a patient's repetitive movement and slots into Spencer's Last Breath to reduce the extra fatigue The Nurse suffers from chaining Blinks. The reduction is substantial enough to feel like a real difference in how many Blinks can be strung together.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaining Blinks without as much fatigue means The Nurse can sustain a longer, more punishing chase without being forced to stop and recover. It is a small but meaningful shift that makes the power feel more continuous and less stop-and-start.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Fit it into a loadout that already strings multiple Blinks together when The Nurse wants to chase for longer without the fatigue penalty dragging her down. The uncommon drop rate makes it an easy find for a build that covers long ground in a single pursuit.

Addon_Chainsaw_001.name: Dad's Boots
Addon_Chainsaw_001.description:
A pair of trusty boots, pulled from the corpse of Max Thompson Sr.

Increases the Chainsaw Sprint turn rate by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: A pair of boots slotted into Chainsaw, borrowed from a dead man's feet, that sharpens the turn rate during the killer's sprint. The chainsaw keeps the same hit and recovery, but the direction change feels quicker.
beginner.whyItMatters: Sharper turning during a sprint lets the killer bend a chase around a corner or loop back on a survivor who tried to cut across open ground. It is a small mobility tweak rather than a power shift, so the chainsaw still plays the same way but with a little extra direction control.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a survivor keeps escaping by cutting through tight indoor spaces or threading between pallets during a chainsaw sprint. The rare drop rate means it will not show up often, so save it when it does appear.

Addon_Chainsaw_002.name: Counterweight
Addon_Chainsaw_002.description:
Adds weight to the base, for stability.

Decreases the Chainsaw Sprints's initial turn rate by 70%.

beginner.whatItIs: Counterweight is a common add-on for Chainsaw that adds mass to the base, making the first turn of a sprint feel slow and wide. The rest of the sprint works normally, so only that opening moment loses its snap.
beginner.whyItMatters: That blunt start means the killer swings into a corner a beat later than expected, giving a survivor an extra heartbeat to break a pallet or vault away. It is a small but consistent drag on the opening move of every chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it only as a deliberate handicap for practice or casual sessions, since in a real match the reduced initial turn works against the killer almost every time a survivor breaks a pallet or vaults. A common drop rate means it will appear frequently enough to notice in the field.

Addon_Chainsaw_003.name: Greased Throttle
Addon_Chainsaw_003.description:
A lubricated trigger. One twitch of the finger brings the chainsaw back to life.

Decreases recovery time after using the Chainsaw by 5%.This effect does not apply while in Overdrive.

beginner.whatItIs: A lubricated trigger slotted into Chainsaw that trims a small amount of recovery time after the killer stops sprinting. The effect pauses while Overdrive is active, so it only helps during the normal recovery window.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster recovery after a sprint means the killer is ready to hit again sooner, which keeps the pressure on during a chase. The small cut and the Overdrive exception make it a light nudge rather than a meaningful shift in how the chainsaw plays out.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a casual build where the killer already has decent chase tempo and wants a tiny extra edge on recovery. Uncommon rarity means it shows up regularly enough to experiment with, so test how the shorter cooldown feels before committing.

Addon_Chainsaw_004.name: Thermal Casing
Addon_Chainsaw_004.description:
A thicker case that allows the user to control the conservation of energy.

Decreases the speed at which the Overdrive meter dissipates when not using the Chainsaw by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Thermal Casing is a thicker case slotted into Chainsaw that slows the drain on the Overdrive meter when the killer is not actively sprinting. The meter still fades, just a bit more gradually than without it.
beginner.whyItMatters: A slower drain means the killer can bank Overdrive charges during quiet stretches and still have them ready when a survivor finally sprints into range. It is a modest pacing change that rewards waiting out a map and striking at the right moment rather than a raw damage increase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if the killer finds the Overdrive meter emptying too fast between chases, especially on larger maps where survivors spread thin. Uncommon rarity keeps it in circulation often enough to build around.

Addon_Chainsaw_005.name: Steel Toe Boots
Addon_Chainsaw_005.description:
Boots with a reinforced toe that offer protection from impact.

Decreases recovery time after hitting an object with the Chainsaw by 10%.

beginner.whatItIs: Steel Toe Boots are reinforced footwear slotted into Chainsaw that cut the recovery time after the killer smashes through an object with the blade. Only the post-impact cooldown shrinks; the hit itself and the sprint are unchanged.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster recovery after breaking a wall or pallet keeps the chainsaw in the killer's hands for the next swing, which matters most in a loop where a survivor keeps breaking obstacles. It is a small responsiveness boost that makes object-breaking feel less punishing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a survivor is camping behind breakable walls or using pallets as a shield during a chase. Common rarity means it will show up often, so it slots easily into any chase-focused setup.

Addon_Chainsaw_006.name: The Thompsons' Mix
Addon_Chainsaw_006.description:
A special oily substance concocted by the family for their machinery.

Decreases recovery time after using the Chainsaw by 10%.This effect does not apply while in Overdrive.

beginner.whatItIs: The Thompsons' Mix is a rare family oil blend slotted into Chainsaw that trims recovery time after the killer stops a sprint. The effect pauses during Overdrive, so it only applies in the standard recovery window.
beginner.whyItMatters: A noticeably shorter recovery after each sprint lets the killer chain hits more fluidly, which keeps a survivor from finding a breather between strikes. It is a meaningful edge for a dedicated chase build, a bigger shift than a small oil add-on would give on its own.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It suits a build that prioritizes long chases over quick repositioning, since the faster recovery keeps the killer in a survivor's face after each vault. The drop rate is low, so save it for a loadout already committed to staying on target.

Addon_Chainsaw_007.name: Begrimed Chains
Addon_Chainsaw_007.description:
A foul yet oddly familiar chain, coated with something unpleasant.

Survivors hit with the Chainsaw suffer from the Mangled and Hemorrhage status effects for 70 seconds.

Hemorrhage regresses healing progress when not healing, and increases blood trails left by injured survivors. This lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

Mangled increases time required to heal by 25% and lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Begrimed Chains is a rare coated chain add-on for the Chainsaw that makes every hit leave two lasting status effects on the survivor. Mangled slows healing while Hemorrhage causes ongoing blood loss and heavier blood trails.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stacking both effects turns a single chainsaw hit into a sustained pressure problem, because the survivor must keep healing to clear Hemorrhage while Mangled makes each healing session take longer. It is a bigger shift than a simple damage tweak, since it changes how a survivor must manage their health for the rest of the match.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a survivor is healing too quickly after a hit and the killer wants to slow that rhythm down. Rare rarity means it will not appear often, so pair it with a chase build that already lands consistent hits to make the most of the double effect.

Addon_Chainsaw_008.name: Ragged Engine
Addon_Chainsaw_008.description:
Some would say it needs a tune-up. Max would say it is tuned-up.

Decreases the speed at which the Overdrive meter dissipates when not using the Chainsaw by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Ragged Engine is a rare worn engine part for Chainsaw that slows the Overdrive meter's drain when the killer is not sprinting. The meter still fades, but at a noticeably slower pace than the stock setup.
beginner.whyItMatters: A slower drain lets the killer stockpile Overdrive through long quiet stretches and still have full charge ready when a survivor finally runs into the open. It is a bigger pacing change than a light drain reduction, rewarding a patient killer who waits for the right moment to strike.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on larger maps where survivors spread thin and the killer has time to build meter between chases. Rare rarity means it will not drop often, so it suits a dedicated Overdrive-focused setup best.

Addon_Chainsaw_009.name: Lo Pro Chains
Addon_Chainsaw_009.description:
Light chains that decrease the weight of the Chainsaw, allowing for greater maneuverability.

Whenever you special-break Pallets or Breakable Walls with the Chainsaw, continue the Chainsaw Sprint.Healthy Survivors hit with the Chainsaw within 5 seconds of breaking Pallet or a Wall are damaged for a single Health State.Injured Survivors suffer from the Deep Wound status effect.

Deep Wound will put a Survivor in the dying state unless it is mended before the timer runs out.

beginner.whatItIs: Lo Pro Chains are very rare lightweight chains for Chainsaw that let the killer continue a sprint after special-breaking a pallet or breakable wall. Survivors hit within a short window after the break take extra damage, and injured survivors suffer Deep Wound.
beginner.whyItMatters: Keeping the sprint alive through a wall or pallet break removes the brief pause that normally gives a survivor a chance to escape, and the follow-up damage punishes them for breaking cover. It is a meaningful shift in chase flow rather than a small stat nudge, because it changes what happens at the exact moment a survivor thinks they have opened a gap.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that relies on breaking obstacles to keep a chase alive, since the continued sprint and bonus damage make every wall break into an extension of the pursuit. Very rare rarity means it will be hard to find, so build the whole chase setup around it once it drops.

Addon_Chainsaw_010.name: Discarded Air Filter
Addon_Chainsaw_010.description:
A cracked and dusty filter. It still manages to work better than the stock model.

Increases the time it takes before the Overdrive meter starts dissipating by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Discarded Air Filter is a common cracked filter for Chainsaw that delays the start of the Overdrive meter's drain. The meter still fades eventually, but it holds its charge a bit longer before the countdown begins.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer grace period before the meter starts to fall gives the killer more leeway to position and wait for a survivor to make a mistake. It is a small pacing tweak that smooths out the rhythm between chases without changing any hit or recovery numbers.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the Overdrive window feels too short to finish a full rotation across the map. Because it appears frequently, it works well as an early pick for anyone testing an Overdrive-focused routine.

Addon_Chainsaw_011.name: Cracked Primer Bulb
Addon_Chainsaw_011.description:
A button that clears air from the fuel lines. This machine needs to be fed.

Survivors hit with the Chainsaw are damaged for a single health state.Increases Overdrive generation by 15%.

beginner.whatItIs: Cracked Primer Bulb is a common small button add-on for Chainsaw that adds a single health state of extra damage to every hit and also boosts Overdrive generation. The hit lands harder and the meter fills faster at the same time.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra damage makes each hit land with more weight, which shortens the number of strikes needed to put a survivor down. The added Overdrive generation rounds out the effect by keeping the sprint meter topped up, making it a solid all-around boost rather than a single-stat nudge.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in any build that wants a bit more punch from the chainsaw without giving up sprint stamina. Common rarity keeps it in the rotation frequently, making it a safe early pick for a new killer setup.

Addon_Chainsaw_012.name: Off-Brand Motor Oil
Addon_Chainsaw_012.description:
Affordable oil that can be used to lubricate noisy chains.

Increases Overdrive generation by 15%.

beginner.whatItIs: Off-Brand Motor Oil is an uncommon affordable lubricant for Chainsaw that increases the rate at which the Overdrive meter builds up during sprints. Nothing else changes; the hit, recovery, and drain all work the same.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster meter generation means the killer can chain sprints more often without waiting for the drain to catch up, which keeps the pressure on during a long chase. It is a small but steady boost that compounds over a full trial, especially on maps with many sprint opportunities.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the Overdrive meter feels like it empties faster than it fills, which is common on open maps with long sprint paths. Uncommon rarity means it will appear regularly, so it is a dependable pick for a sprint-heavy setup.

ADDON_Chainsaw_CarburatorGuide.name: Tuned Carburetor
ADDON_Chainsaw_CarburatorGuide.description:
Despite being caked in dirt and oil, this carburetor has been well adjusted.

Increases Chainsaw charge speed by 20%.Decreases base movement speed to 4.4 m/s.

beginner.whatItIs: Trades base movement speed for a faster Chainsaw charge rate, so the saw is ready sooner but the killer moves slower in exchange. The swap is deliberate and visible in how the killer gets around.
beginner.whyItMatters: Quicker access to the saw's burst rewards plays built around a well-timed Overdrive, even if everyday mobility suffers. That is a trade rather than a flat improvement.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on iridescent rolls if the approach is built on charging the saw and letting it decide the chase. It fits a slower, deliberate killer who values a fast Overdrive over raw top speed.

ADDON_Chainsaw_DeathEngravings.name: Clogged Intake
ADDON_Chainsaw_DeathEngravings.description:
Modifying the airflow is key to modifying the saw’s power.

Increases Overdrive duration by 15%.

beginner.whatItIs: Stretches the duration of the Chainsaw's Overdrive state, keeping it active for longer once it starts. The charged window simply lasts more.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer Overdrive gives the killer more time to act on a fully charged saw, which can turn a missed window into another chance. It reads as a meaningful change to the power's timing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on uncommon rolls when the Overdrive feels too short to act on. Good for a killer who wants the charged state to linger long enough to finish the job.

ADDON_Chainsaw_DoomEngravings.name: Iridescent Engravings
ADDON_Chainsaw_DoomEngravings.description:
Engravings found on the Chainsaw body representing the dark beast that lives in The Fog. Fills the user with determination.

Increases Chainsaw Sprint movement speed by 20%.Increases time required to charge the Chainsaw by 12%.

beginner.whatItIs: Boosts Chainsaw Sprint movement speed at the cost of a slower charge rate, so the saw is faster to ride but takes longer to build. The trade shifts when the killer can commit to a sprint.
beginner.whyItMatters: Each Overdrive feels quicker to ride, but the buildup takes more patience, which changes the rhythm of committing to a chase. That is a trade, not a simple improvement.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on iridescent rolls if long chases feel sluggish. Good for a speed-first killer who values momentum over a fast charge-up.

ADDON_Chainsaw_HomemadeMuffler.name: Apex Muffler
ADDON_Chainsaw_HomemadeMuffler.description:
A masterfully crafted chainsaw muffler that outperforms all others.

Chainsaw is silent for Survivors outside the Terror Radius.

beginner.whatItIs: Muffles the Chainsaw's engine so survivors outside the Terror Radius can no longer hear it running. The sound that usually gives away the killer's position simply stops.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the engine noise hides the killer's approach, so survivors lose a key cue for keeping their distance. That is a big shift in how the chase sounds to the other side.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Grab it on very rare rolls when position awareness is a problem. It fits a killer who wants to close from a direction survivors cannot hear.

ADDON_Chainsaw_LightChassis.name: Low Kickback Chains
ADDON_Chainsaw_LightChassis.description:
A specialized chain that reduces the likelihood of kickback.

Decreases recovery time after hitting an object with the Chainsaw by 15%.

beginner.whatItIs: Cuts the recovery time after the Chainsaw hits an object, letting the killer re-engage sooner. The dead time after a blocked swing simply shrinks.
beginner.whyItMatters: Less downtime after a blocked swing means the killer can press the chase again quickly, which matters around pallets and tight loops. It reads as a small but useful tweak to flow.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on rare rolls if wasted recovery time keeps ending chases. Good when the killer often meets walls or survivors mid-swing.

ADDON_Chainsaw_ThompsonMix.name: High-Speed Idler Screw
ADDON_Chainsaw_ThompsonMix.description:
A loosened screw will bring more power to the chainsaw.

Increases the time it takes before the Overdrive meter starts dissipating by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Slows the rate at which the Overdrive meter drains after it fills, so the charge lingers. The saw stays ready for a wider window.
beginner.whyItMatters: A slower drain keeps the saw charged longer, giving the killer a wider window to commit to a chase. That is a meaningful shift in how long the reward lasts.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on uncommon rolls when the charge feels like it vanishes too fast. Good for a killer who wants the saw ready through a full generator loop.

ADDON_Chainsaw_ThompsonMoonshine.name: Spiked Boots
ADDON_Chainsaw_ThompsonMoonshine.description:
Boots with strapped-on pieces of metal which burrow in mud for more stability and control with each step.

Increases the Chainsaw Sprint turn rate by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Sharpens the turn rate while Chainsaw Sprinting, so the killer tracks tighter around corners. The saw follows the killer's direction more closely at speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Sharper turning lets the killer keep up with a looping survivor more reliably, which matters on maps with tight generator loops. That is a real change to chase handling.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on very rare rolls if chases around corners feel sloppy. Good for a killer who values tracking a survivor through tight spaces.

Addon_Demogorgon_BarbsGlasses.name: Barb's Glasses
Addon_Demogorgon_BarbsGlasses.description:
A broken pair of glasses that traveled to the Upside Down.

Whenever you special-break Pallets or Breakable Walls with Shred, the cooldown is 10% shorter

beginner.whatItIs: Barb's Glasses are an uncommon broken eyewear add-on for Of the Abyss that shortens the cooldown after a successful Shred hit on a pallet or breakable wall. The Shred miss cooldown is untouched, so only clean hits benefit.
beginner.whyItMatters: A shorter post-hit cooldown lets the killer keep breaking obstacles in quick succession, which matters when a survivor is using a loop of pallets to stall the chase. It is a small tempo boost that makes the Shred feel snappier in a sustained exchange.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that leans on Shred to break through obstacles and keep a chase alive through indoor or pallet-heavy loops. Uncommon rarity means it will show up often enough to experiment with in different setups.

Addon_Demogorgon_BlackHeart.name: Black Heart
Addon_Demogorgon_BlackHeart.description:
A black fermented heart ripped from the chest of a tentacled creature in the Upside Down.

Decreases Shred hit cooldown by 10%.

beginner.whatItIs: Black Heart is a common dark organ add-on for Of the Abyss that reduces the cooldown after a successful Shred hit. It targets the hit-side cooldown specifically, leaving the miss cooldown unchanged.
beginner.whyItMatters: A faster recovery between successful Shred hits keeps the killer's momentum going through a sequence of pallet breaks, which is exactly the moment a survivor hopes the chase will stall. It is a small but consistent tempo improvement that compounds over the course of a full trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it as a low-cost way to smooth out the Shred rhythm without needing a rare drop. Common rarity means it will appear frequently, so it is an easy first add-on to slot into a new Of the Abyss setup.

Addon_Demogorgon_BrassCaseLighter.name: Brass Case Lighter
Addon_Demogorgon_BrassCaseLighter.description:
A lighter used to ignite trouble.

Proximity to Portals inflicts Survivors with Blindness. Once out of contact with the Portal, this effect persists for 60 seconds.

Blindness prevents Survivors from seeing auras.

beginner.whatItIs: A brass lighter slotted into Of the Abyss that inflicts Blindness on survivors who come near a Portal. The effect lingers for a short time after the survivor steps out of the portal's reach, blocking their view of auras.
beginner.whyItMatters: Losing aura vision right after leaving a portal forces survivors to guess where the killer is emerging, which breaks their ability to play safely from a distance. It is a meaningful information shift because it turns the portal zone into a dangerous blind spot for anyone passing through.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It shines in matches where survivors lean heavily on aura vision to path around portals and slip away. Because it is a rare find, fold it into a portal-zone plan and let the lingering blindness punish survivors who rely on reading auras near the entry point.

Addon_Demogorgon_DeerLung.name: Deer Lung
Addon_Demogorgon_DeerLung.description:
A raw, rubbery lung that reinvigorates The Demogorgon.

Increases Upside Down movement speed by 30%.Decreases the number of available Portals by 2.

beginner.whatItIs: Deer Lung is a rare raw lung add-on for Of the Abyss that increases the killer's movement speed while traversing the Upside Down. In exchange, two portals are removed from the map, shrinking the available network.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster travel through the Upside Down means the killer can cross the map and re-emerge near a survivor much more quickly, which changes the tempo of every pursuit. Losing two portals is a real trade-off, making the overall effect a bigger shift in routing options rather than a simple speed bump.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it when fast traversal matters more than having every portal available on the map. It is a rare drop, so it fits best into a setup that already has a fixed set of preferred routes and does not need the full portal count.

Addon_Demogorgon_ElevensSoda.name: Eleven's Soda
Addon_Demogorgon_ElevensSoda.description:
A soda can charged with psychic energy.

Shows Auras for Generators being repaired while traversing the Upside Down.

beginner.whatItIs: Eleven's Soda is a rare charged soda can add-on for Of the Abyss that reveals the auras of generators being repaired while the killer traverses the Upside Down. The information is only visible during the traverse, not on the surface.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing which generators survivors are working on while underground lets the killer emerge directly on top of them, cutting into healing progress and forcing a rescue. It is a meaningful information shift that turns the Upside Down from a blind tunnel into a targeted scouting lane.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors scatter across the map and the killer needs to locate active generator work without wandering blind through the Upside Down. It drops rarely, so pair it with a routing plan that funnels traverses toward the areas where repair activity is most likely.

Addon_Demogorgon_LerproseLichen.name: Leprose Lichen
Addon_Demogorgon_LerproseLichen.description:
A potent lichen that grows like dust on the rocks in the Upside Down.

Reveals the auras of all Survivors while traversing the Upside Down.After emerging from a Portal, the auras of all Survivors within 16 meters of an active Portal are revealed for 3 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Leprose Lichen slots into Of the Abyss and keeps every survivor's aura lit while the killer moves through the Upside Down. Emerging from a portal also exposes the auras of survivors standing close to that portal for a short moment.
beginner.whyItMatters: Full survivor visibility underground turns the Upside Down into a complete information lane, letting the killer choose the exact emergence point that will catch a survivor off guard. The brief post-emergence reveal adds a second beat of tracking, making it a bigger vision shift than a simple aura flash.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It rewards a playstyle that treats the Upside Down as a primary scouting tool, since the constant aura feed makes every traversal productive. Because it is an iridescent find and not one to expect regularly, treat it as the centerpiece of a vision-driven loadout.

Addon_Demogorgon_LifeguardWhistle.name: Lifeguard Whistle
Addon_Demogorgon_LifeguardWhistle.description:
A rusty, metal whistle that once ruled the Hawkins public pool.

Increases the number of available Portals by 2.

beginner.whatItIs: Lifeguard Whistle is a very rare rusty whistle add-on for Of the Abyss that adds two extra portals to the map. The extra openings expand the network of routes the killer can take through the Upside Down.
beginner.whyItMatters: More portals means more repositioning options, which lets the killer pop up in places survivors do not expect and escape from a bad position through the other dimension. It is a map-control shift rather than a stat change, because it reshapes the geometry of the entire trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it to maps where the default portal placement feels cramped or too predictable, because the extra openings create fresh chase corridors and repositioning angles. It is a very rare find, so build a portal-routing plan around it the moment it appears.

Addon_Demogorgon_MewsGuts.name: Mew's Guts
Addon_Demogorgon_MewsGuts.description:
The tasty guts of an unfortunate victim.

Increases the total number of available Portals by 1.Decreases Shred miss cooldown by 11%.

beginner.whatItIs: An uncommon slot for Of the Abyss that grants an extra portal on the map and trims the recovery window after a whiffed Shred swing. The pairing keeps the killer repositioning faster and opens another exit option mid-chase.
beginner.whyItMatters: A faster recovery after a whiffed Shred keeps the killer in the fight instead of standing idle, while the extra portal gives an additional escape or approach route. Together they are two small nudges that make the overall flow of a chase feel smoother and less interrupted.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if the killer often wastes time after a missed Shred or feels locked into too few portal routes. Uncommon rarity means it will show up regularly, so it is a safe early pick for a new Of the Abyss build.

Addon_Demogorgon_RatLiver.name: Rat Liver
Addon_Demogorgon_RatLiver.description: A soggy pile of salty, soft liver.Increases movement speed while charging Of The Abyss by 3.5%.

beginner.whatItIs: Rat Liver slots into Of the Abyss. It gives The Demogorgon a small movement speed boost while the power is being channeled toward a survivor.
beginner.whyItMatters: That extra pace during the channel helps close the final stretch of distance before a survivor slips behind cover or a pallet. It keeps the attack from whiffing when the target is just barely out of range.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in chases where The Demogorgon is already within the channel range and just needs a little more speed to finish the approach. It is common, so it will appear in the addon cache regularly.

Addon_Demogorgon_RatTail.name: Rat Tail
Addon_Demogorgon_RatTail.description: A chewy rat tail for The Demogorgon to consume.Increases speed of opening a Portal by 50%.

beginner.whatItIs: Rat Tail slots into Of the Abyss. It speeds up how quickly a Portal opens when The Demogorgon activates it, shrinking the vulnerable pause before stepping through.
beginner.whyItMatters: A faster portal opening means less time exposed where survivors can seal the gate or land a hit. Each traversal feels snappier and harder to interrupt because the window of vulnerability is tighter.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors are camping near a Portal and The Demogorgon needs to slip through before they can react. Its common rarity means it is easy to find at the addon bench.

Addon_Demogorgon_RedMoss.name: Red Moss
Addon_Demogorgon_RedMoss.description:
A psychedelic moss that grows on tree barks in the Upside Down.

Increases time required to emerge from a Portal by 15%.Increases the duration of the Undetectable effect gained when emerging from a Portal by 8 seconds.Emerging from Portals becomes silent.

Undetectable hides the Killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain.

beginner.whatItIs: Red Moss slots into Of the Abyss and changes three things at once. The Demogorgon takes slightly longer to emerge from a Portal, the Undetectable window after emerging is extended, and the emergence itself becomes completely silent.
beginner.whyItMatters: The silence plus the longer stealth stretch turn each portal hop into a repositioning opportunity rather than a noisy tell. That is a meaningful shift in how traversal plays out compared to the default audible exit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the trial rewards sneaking around generators or looping behind survivors instead of a direct chase. As an iridescent drop it is rare enough to save for a match where stealth repositioning is the whole plan.

Addon_Demogorgon_RottenGreenTripe.name: Rotten Green Tripe
Addon_Demogorgon_RottenGreenTripe.description: Rotten tripe that fuels The Demogorgon.Increases Upside Down movement speed by 15%.

beginner.whatItIs: Rotten Green Tripe slots into Of the Abyss. It adds a noticeable movement speed increase while The Demogorgon is inside the Upside Down plane, making the transit between two Portals feel faster end to end.
beginner.whyItMatters: Closing the gap between entering one Portal and emerging from the other reduces the window where a survivor can call for help or seal the destination gate. The traversal itself becomes less of a committed gamble.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it on maps where the two Portal locations are far apart and the transit takes a good chunk of the match. Its uncommon rarity keeps it from appearing in every cache.

Addon_Demogorgon_RottenPumpkin.name: Rotten Pumpkin
Addon_Demogorgon_RottenPumpkin.description:
Pumpkin flesh infected by the rotten soil in Hawkins.

When traversing the Upside Down, the Portal you enter is destroyed. Gain an additional 200 Bloodpoints for the traversal.

beginner.whatItIs: Rotten Pumpkin slots into Of the Abyss. When The Demogorgon traverses through a Portal, the Portal it enters is destroyed and the traversal grants a chunk of bonus Bloodpoints.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing a Portal on arrival stops survivors from using that same spot to chase The Demogorgon back. The Bloodpoint payout also makes frequent traversal feel like it pays off in score by the end of the trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when survivors keep looping through the same Portal to reposition and The Demogorgon wants to shut that lane down. It is common, so it shows up often enough to build a habit around.

Addon_Demogorgon_StickyLining.name: Sticky Lining
Addon_Demogorgon_StickyLining.description:
A fetid, viscous layer that covers and expands the interdimensional tunnels.

Increases the distance from Portals at which Survivors can be detected by Of The Abyss by 2.5 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: Sticky Lining slots into Of the Abyss. It extends the range at which the power can sense survivors near a Portal, widening the detection bubble around each gateway.
beginner.whyItMatters: That extra reach means a survivor hiding just outside the normal detection ring still gets marked. It closes the gap between a safe perch and a spotted one without changing anything else about the power.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors in the trial keep camping at the edge of a Portal and The Demogorgon needs a wider net to flush them out. It is uncommon, so expect to wait a bit for it in the cache.

Addon_Demogorgon_ThornyVines.name: Thorny Vines
Addon_Demogorgon_ThornyVines.description:
Thick, thorny vines that stretch and reinforce the interdimensional tunnels.
