beginner.whatItIs: Any survivor struck by a thrown axe immediately suffers Hemorrhage and Mangled on top of the base hit. An uncommon Fazbear's Fright slot-in, it makes direct axe contact a compounding injury that drags out healing and bleeds trail visibility.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stacking both effects on a hit makes healing slower and blood trails thicker, so a landed axe becomes a real threat to a survivor's recovery. It is a bigger commitment to punishing hits than a small speed tweak.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants clean axe hits to wreck a survivor's ability to heal and escape. It is uncommon, so it fits aggressive axe play well.

Addon_K40_06.name: Greasy Paper Plate
Addon_K40_06.description:
It sticks to everything it touches. No amount of soap can wash it off.

Increases the time required for Survivors to remove the Axe by 15%.

beginner.whatItIs: A common slot for Fazbear's Fright that stretches the time a survivor needs to remove an embedded axe. The added drag turns a brief delay into a meaningful stretch of the chase.
beginner.whyItMatters: Extra seconds of stuck-ness gives the killer more room to track the axe aura and re-engage before the survivor frees up. It is a reliable pressure tool that extends every successful hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants landed axes to linger and keep the chase alive. It is common, so it is a dependable fit for most builds.

Addon_K40_07.name: Streamers
Addon_K40_07.description:
Employees would throw them over the rafters for a quick decoration.

Increases the speed at which you travel through Security Doors by 15%.

beginner.whatItIs: An uncommon upgrade to Fazbear's Fright that quickens the killer's passage through Security Doors. The snappier crossing keeps chase momentum alive instead of stalling at every wall.
beginner.whyItMatters: Moving through doors faster keeps the killer's momentum going across the map and shortens the gap between chases. It is a clean tempo boost for a power built on teleporting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants to cross the map and re-engage with less downtime in each door. It is uncommon, so it is a good fit for aggressive teleport play.

Addon_K40_08.name: Party Hat
Addon_K40_08.description:
The party never ends, no matter how much they beg.

When an Axe is embedded in the environment:Increases its area of effect radius to 250% over 3 seconds.Decreases the duration of the area of effect by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: An uncommon add-on for Fazbear's Fright that expands the axe's area of effect into a much wider zone once embedded. The broader zone fades quicker than usual, trading lasting coverage for a short burst of reach.
beginner.whyItMatters: A wider, briefer zone catches more survivors in the axe's reach but burns out sooner, trading coverage for a tighter window. It is a bigger shift in how the zone reads than a simple duration tweak.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants the axe zone to sweep a wider area around a cluster of survivors. It is uncommon, so it is a solid pick for zone-heavy play.

Addon_K40_09.name: Office Phone
Addon_K40_09.description:
He tried to leave messages as a warning. He didn't last long, either.

Survivors within 24 meters of a Survivor with an embedded Axe gain the Oblivious and - if injured - Broken status effects. Reveals the aura of the Axe to Survivors within this range.

Decreases the time required to remove the Axe from another Survivor by 50%.

Oblivious prevents Survivors from hearing or being affected by the Killer's Terror Radius.

Broken prevents Survivors from being healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Fitting into Fazbear's Fright, it marks every survivor caught near an embedded axe as Oblivious and adds Broken to any of them who are already injured. The zone also exposes the axe's own aura and cuts the removal time for a teammate's axe in half.
beginner.whyItMatters: Muting terror radius and blocking healing around a hooked survivor makes the axe an anchor that punishes nearby helpers, while revealing the axe's aura and speeding teammate removal add a layer of paranoia to the cluster. It is a big shift in how an embedded axe reads to everyone nearby.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the map setup clusters survivors near each other and the killer can land an axe on one to ripple control outward. It is uncommon, so it suits builds that punish tight grouping rather than single-target pursuit.

Addon_K40_10.name: Chica’s Bib
Addon_K40_10.description:
A good way to keep Mr. Cupcake from making a mess.

Survivors within the Axe's area of effect gain the Exhausted status effect for 5 seconds.

Exhausted prevents Survivors from activating exhausting perks.

beginner.whatItIs: Slotting into Fazbear's Fright, it washes every survivor caught inside the axe's zone with Exhausted, locking them out of exhausting perks. The effect removes a critical escape option at exactly the moment a chase tightens.
beginner.whyItMatters: Exhausted survivors cannot activate their exhausting perks, which strips escape tools the instant they land in the zone. It is a meaningful shift that weakens a survivor's counterplay at the exact moment of danger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when survivors lean heavily on exhausting perks to break away and the killer can pin them under the axe zone. It is rare, so it rewards setups where the axe lands in a spot survivors must cross.

Addon_K40_11.name: Bonnie’s Guitar Strings
Addon_K40_11.description:
Worn strings that are off-tune and liable to snap.

Unlocks potential in one’s aura reading ability.

While moving between Security Doors, the repair progress of generators can be determined by the intensity of their auras.

Decreases the duration of the Undetectable status effect upon exiting the Security Door by 100%.

Undetectable hides the Killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain.

beginner.whatItIs: Fitting into Fazbear's Fright, it lets the killer judge how far along a generator is by reading the strength of its aura during Security Door transit. Exiting a door also wipes the Undetectable status clean, so the invisible streak ends the instant the crossing finishes.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reading generator progress by aura intensity while shuttling between doors lets the killer prioritize targets with real clarity, but it fully removes the stealth normally gained after each exit. It is a bigger trade than a simple information perk, swapping invisibility for map awareness.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer values tracking generator progress over the stealth that a door exit normally provides. It is rare, so it rewards aggressive information play.

Addon_K40_12.name: Foxy’s Hook
Addon_K40_12.description:
A pirate’s hook that seems more menacing than playful.

Players within range of the Axe's area of effect gain 7% Haste for 6 seconds.

Haste increases Killer movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Fazbear's Fright picks up a short burst of extra speed whenever its axe zone overlaps a survivor. The added pace helps the killer close the gap while a target is still trapped in the radius.
beginner.whyItMatters: A speed kick during the axe's zone lets the killer close gaps and re-engage while survivors are still under pressure. It is a clean tempo boost that pairs well with aggressive axe play.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants to stay fast and mobile while the axe zone is active. It is rare, so it fits fast, chase-heavy play.

Addon_K40_13.name: Purple Guy Drawing
Addon_K40_13.description:
He only takes 10 seconds to draw!

While a Survivor has an Axe embedded in them, any rushed interactions they perform reveal their aura to you for 3 seconds.

Removing the Axe from themselves reveals their aura to you for 6 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Its axe mechanic gains a new layer of information. While a survivor carries an embedded axe, any rushed interaction they attempt briefly exposes their location, and pulling the axe out of their own body stretches that exposure window further.
beginner.whyItMatters: A rushed action by a hooked survivor flashes their location, and even pulling the axe off themselves reveals them, so every desperate move under the axe becomes readable. It is a meaningful shift that punishes panic and rewards patient tracking.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants hooked survivors to be punished for rushing any action while the axe is in them. It is rare, so it rewards information-driven play.

Addon_K40_14.name: Freddy’s Hat
Addon_K40_14.description:
Gabriel trusted the wrong grown-up. Now he's the star of the show.

Increases the Axe's weight while throwing by 100%.

beginner.whatItIs: Freddy's Hat slots into Fazbear's Fright and gives the Axe noticeably more weight while it is in flight. The heavier projectile changes the feel of every throw.
beginner.whyItMatters: A heavier projectile carries more momentum through the map and feels less like a tossed token, which shifts the power from quick flicks into committed throws. It reads as a small tweak to how the weapon travels rather than a full redesign of its kit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in trials where the Axe's range feels short or where the embedded state is harder to sidestep. It is a rare find, so reserve the slot for it when building around committed Axe throws.

Addon_K40_15.name: Loot Bag
Addon_K40_15.description:
Open the bag, and see what goodies are inside.

While a Survivor has an Axe embedded in them: Exit gates will be blocked for them and any Survivors within 12 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: Loot Bag slots into Fazbear's Fright and blocks Exit Gates for a survivor who has the Axe stuck in them. Anyone nearby shares the same restriction while the effect persists.
beginner.whyItMatters: Locking the exits while a Survivor is impaled removes the usual escape route and forces the remaining group to keep working or risk being cut off. It is a meaningful shift in late-trial pressure rather than a small stat bump.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the lobby has heavy Exit Gate usage or when the group tends to split near the exits in the late game. Very rare drops make it a prize, so pair it with a killer build that already punishes late-trial clustering.

Addon_K40_16.name: Access Panel
Addon_K40_16.description:
Gaining control over the security doors is key to getting the job done.

Your Axe gains the ability to travel through Security Doors, and will exit straight through the connected Security Door.

When aiming your Axe:Gain Killer Instinct on Survivors within 6 meters of any Security Door.Reveals the auras of all Security Door numbers.

beginner.whatItIs: Access Panel slots into Fazbear's Fright and lets the Axe pass through Security Doors to land on the connected side. While aiming, the killer sees the numbers on every door and gains Killer Instinct on survivors close to any of them.
beginner.whyItMatters: The ability to thread the Axe through a sealed door removes a layer of map control that survivors rely on, and the aura reveal turns Security Door positioning into a guessing game. It is a bigger shift because it changes how the power interacts with the map's layout rather than just one stat.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on maps with many Security Doors or in lobbies where the group camps behind sealed passages. The very rare drop rate makes it a long-term prize, so slot it into a build that already leans on Axe positioning.

Addon_K40_17.name: Celebrate! Poster
Addon_K40_17.description:
The celebration lasts all night long, or until no one is left.

While the Axe is embedded in a Survivor, all players within 32 meters gain 12% Haste and vault 20% faster.

Haste increases Killer movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Celebrate! Poster slots into Fazbear's Fright and grants Haste to everyone in the area for as long as the Axe remains embedded in a survivor. Vaulting also becomes quicker during that window, affecting both sides.
beginner.whyItMatters: The temporary speed boost lets a chase build close gaps faster and clear vaults quicker during the window a Survivor is stuck. It is a moderate change that rewards the moment of embedding rather than the approach to it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in lobbies where vault-heavy escape routes are common, since the extra movement speed shrinks the time between a hit and a locked-down Survivor. Its very rare rarity makes it a reward for patience in the offering pool.

Addon_K40_18.name: Faz-Coin
Addon_K40_18.description:
Collecting these tokens comes with a price.

Upon throwing the Axe, it gains a Terror Radius of 24 meters until it is reclaimed. You gain the Undetectable status effect for 10 seconds.

Undetectable hides the Killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain.

beginner.whatItIs: Faz-Coin slots into Fazbear's Fright and projects a Terror Radius from the thrown Axe until it is reclaimed. The moment of release also makes the killer briefly Undetectable, concealing their aura and red stain.
beginner.whyItMatters: The Terror Radius punishes survivors who hover near an embedded Axe, while the short stealth window lets the killer reposition without being tracked by aura. It is a bigger shift because it adds two distinct layers of pressure to a single throw.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in chases where breaking line of sight quickly after throwing is critical, or where survivors camp near the Axe waiting for it to come free. Iridescent drops are uncommon enough that slotting it replaces a more common option, so weigh that trade-off.

Addon_K40_19.name: Endo CPU
Addon_K40_19.description:
Greater computing power, for greater efficacy.

Within the Axe's area of effect, you basic-break Pallets or Breakable Walls, and damage Generators 40% faster. This effect lingers for 5 seconds after leaving the area of effect.

beginner.whatItIs: It slots into Fazbear's Fright and lets the killer break pallets and breakable walls using a normal hit while standing inside the axe's area of effect. Generators caught in that same zone take extra damage from the killer, so their repair progress gets knocked back faster rather than survivors repairing them any quicker. That damage boost keeps applying for a short stretch even after the killer steps out of the zone.
beginner.whyItMatters: Turning the Axe's zone into a repair-punishment tool lets the killer deny safe work spots from a distance and pressure generators without closing in fully. It is a moderate shift that adds a secondary job to the power without replacing its main loop.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in lobbies where generator racing is fast and the group repairs in tight clusters near pallets. The effect lingers briefly after leaving the zone, so use it to apply pressure just before the Axe is reclaimed rather than waiting for a clean hit.

Addon_K40_20.name: Iridescent Remnant
Addon_K40_20.description:
Molten metal - in the right hands, it's the key to immortality.

When you start moving to a Security Door, upright pallets within 32 meters of the destination Door are blocked for 12 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Iridescent Remnant slots into Fazbear's Fright and locks upright pallets around the Security Door the killer is heading toward. The block reshapes the immediate area and denies those drop spots for a short window.
beginner.whyItMatters: Locking pallets near the destination door removes the drop spots survivors depend on to break line of sight, so chases reaching an exit feel tighter and more dangerous. The effect reshapes local map geometry for a brief window, a larger swing in play than a single stat adjustment.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on maps with long corridor sections or where pallet-heavy loops guard the way to the doors. The iridescent rarity means it is a long-term find, so pair it with a build that already pressures Security Door areas.

Addon_K41_01.name: Sticky Lozenge
Addon_K41_01.description:
A simple tablet to moisten a dry throat, often taken before an audition.

When charging Regurgitate, see a preview of the impact zone.

beginner.whatItIs: Sticky Lozenge slots into Unbodied Flesh and displays a preview of where the Regurgitate impact zone will land while the charge is still building. A clear target area makes it easier to commit to a placement rather than guessing where the blob will land.
beginner.whyItMatters: Seeing the landing spot ahead of time removes the guesswork from a power that rewards precision, making it easier to line up hits in tight spaces. It is a small quality-of-life tweak rather than a stat change.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it whenever learning the timing of Regurgitate, since the visual preview builds muscle memory faster than trial and error alone. Its common rarity makes it an easy early pick with no downside to holding.

Addon_K41_02.name: Broken Tiara
Addon_K41_02.description:
A dazzling stage prop worn by a pharaoh's daughter, as distracting as it is fake.

Survivors are Oblivious under the Glowing Fungus' effect.

Oblivious prevents Survivors from hearing or being affected by the Killer's Terror Radius.

beginner.whatItIs: Broken Tiara slots into Unbodied Flesh and applies the Oblivious status to survivors caught under the Glowing Fungus effect. While Oblivious, those survivors cannot hear or be affected by the killer's Terror Radius.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing Terror Radius awareness from an infected survivor blinds them to the killer's approach, turning what would be an early-warning moment into a surprise. It is a moderate shift because it strips one of the survivor's core awareness tools while the fungus is active.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in lobbies where survivors lean heavily on Terror Radius for map awareness, since the fungus now erases that signal entirely. It is common enough to grab early and pairs well with any build that spreads Glowing Fungi quickly.

Addon_K41_03.name: Luckless Mouse
Addon_K41_03.description:
A game of cat and mouse always gets the blood pumping.

Increases Headlong Flight's charges by 2.

beginner.whatItIs: Luckless Mouse slots into Unbodied Flesh and grants Headlong Flight additional charges to spend during a trial. The extra dashes extend the window where the killer can close gaps or break line of sight.
beginner.whyItMatters: More charges mean the dash can be used more often in a single chase or across multiple chases without waiting for a long recharge. It is a small but reliable tweak that smooths out the power's cooldown gaps.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in lobbies where chases tend to drag on or where multiple survivors force repeated engagements. Common rarity means it is easy to acquire, so it is a safe default for a Unbodied Flesh build still being shaped.

Addon_K41_04.name: First Libretto
Addon_K41_04.description:
She felt as if she could walk on the air after landing a role in her first opera.

Decreases Headlong Flight's consumption rate by 30% for 15 seconds any time you hook a Leeched Survivor.

beginner.whatItIs: First Libretto slots into Unbodied Flesh and slows how quickly Headlong Flight charges drain once a Leeched survivor is hooked. The extended window lets the killer stretch those charges further between engagements.
beginner.whyItMatters: The temporary reduction in consumption keeps the dash ready longer in the moments right after a hook, when follow-up pressure matters most. It is a modest tweak that rewards a specific kill-window rather than changing the power's baseline.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in lobbies where hook-to-chase transitions are common, since the brief efficiency boost lines up with the moment after a downed survivor is placed. Its common drop rate makes it a low-risk pick for a Unbodied Flesh kit.

Addon_K41_05.name: Wriggling Parasite
Addon_K41_05.description:
A fragile organism that has an unusual effect on its host.

Increases the passive growth rate to Leeched II by 16%.

beginner.whatItIs: Wriggling Parasite slots into Unbodied Flesh and accelerates the passive growth of the Leeched state toward its later tier. Reaching the stronger Leeched stage with less active pressure gives the killer more room to reposition between hooks.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster progression through the Leeched tiers means the killer's pressure on a survivor escalates sooner after the initial mark is applied. It is a small tweak that shortens the time between infection and maximum effect.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in lobbies where the group camps generators and survives long, since the accelerated growth punishes slow play harder. Uncommon rarity means it is a step up from the common options without being a rare find.

Addon_K41_06.name: Chunk of Malai
Addon_K41_06.description:
A varied source of protein contributes to good gut health.

Decreases the Glowing Fungus' cleanse rate by 8% for each Leeched Survivor.

beginner.whatItIs: An add-on for Unbodied Flesh that slows how quickly survivors purge the Glowing Fungus debuff. Each survivor carrying the Leeched state adds another layer of resistance, so the debuff lingers longer on the map.
beginner.whyItMatters: The more survivors carrying the Leeched mark, the harder it is for any of them to shake off the fungus, creating a compounding pressure loop. It is a moderate shift because the effect scales with how much of the killer's infection kit is already active.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in lobbies where the group stays clustered and shares the map, since each additional Leeched survivor makes the fungus stickier for everyone. Its uncommon rarity puts it just above the easy common picks, so slot it once the core build is set.

Addon_K41_07.name: Crumpled Sheet Music
Addon_K41_07.description:
Before her desperation, she hoped that continued practice would be enough to succeed.

Gain 12 charges to Headlong Flight when a Survivor is hit by a Leeching Gland.

beginner.whatItIs: A slot-in for Unbodied Flesh that dumps a large burst of Headlong Flight charges the moment a survivor is struck by a Leeching Gland. It rewards landing hits with immediate mobility, keeping the dash ready for the next engagement.
beginner.whyItMatters: The charge burst arrives exactly when the killer has just opened a chase, giving the dash extra uses at the most important moment. It is a moderate shift that rewards a clean gland hit by unlocking more follow-up pressure.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in lobbies where opening chases tend to stall after the first hit, since the extra charges keep the dash available through the full pursuit. Uncommon rarity makes it a solid mid-tier pick for a Unbodied Flesh kit.

Addon_K41_08.name: Defective Metronome
Addon_K41_08.description:
The metronome sparks as it plays at a frenetic pace.

Survivors under the Glowing Fungus' effect are Exhausted.

Exhausted prevents Survivors from activating certain perks.

beginner.whatItIs: Slots into Unbodied Flesh and applies the Exhausted state to any survivor sitting under the Glowing Fungus debuff. Exhausted locks out certain perk activations, so affected survivors lose access to key tools mid-chase.
beginner.whyItMatters: Exhausting an infected survivor locks out any perk that needs an Exhausted-free state to trigger, stripping away a key escape tool right when a chase heats up. Paired with everything else the fungus already does, it turns a simple infection into a multi-layer debuff that keeps piling on pressure.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in lobbies where survivors stack strong utility perks, since the Exhausted state neutralizes those perks while the fungus is active. Its uncommon rarity makes it a worthwhile upgrade once the basic Unbodied Flesh setup is in place.

Addon_K41_09.name: Pig's Eye
Addon_K41_09.description:
It still glistens with saliva.

When a Survivor eats a Glowing Fungus from further than 40 meters away, their aura is revealed to you for 6 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Attaches to Unbodied Flesh and exposes a survivor's aura for a short window whenever they consume a Glowing Fungus from far away. The reveal only triggers when the distance between eater and fungus is large enough, making it a tool for tracking survivors who pick food from across the map.
beginner.whyItMatters: The aura reveal punishes survivors who try to manage the fungus from a safe distance, turning a quiet self-care moment into a tracking opportunity. It is a small but targeted tweak that rewards the killer's patience in reading the map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in lobbies where survivors keep their distance and clear fungi from cover, since the reveal turns their safety into exposure. Uncommon rarity makes it a reliable mid-tier pick for a Unbodied Flesh build.

Addon_K41_10.name: Chicken Head
Addon_K41_10.description:
Believed by some to have mystical properties, this particular sample was lodged in the Krasue's throat after a feed.

All Survivors start afflicted with Leeched I.2 additional Glowing Fungi are spawned at the start of the trial.

beginner.whatItIs: Iridescent add-on for Unbodied Flesh that drops every survivor into the early Leeched tier the instant the trial begins. The map also spawns extra Glowing Fungi at the start, giving the power more fuel to work with from the opening moment.
beginner.whyItMatters: Beginning the match with the infection already active removes the buildup phase and forces survivors to deal with the Leeched state from the first generator. The extra fungi also give the killer more spread to work with early on. It is a bigger shift because it rewrites the opening tempo of the power.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in lobbies where the group rushes generators before the killer establishes a pattern, since the pre-applied pressure disrupts that early momentum. Iridescent rarity makes it a long-term prize, so build the rest of the kit around the faster infection curve.

Addon_K41_11.name: Janjira's Hand
Addon_K41_11.description:
One of the few distinguishable parts that remained of her friend.

Gain 2 Headlong Flight charges whenever a generator is repaired. Headlong Flight's recharge rate is increased by 25% for 15 seconds.When 5 generators are repaired, Headlong Flight is fully charged and the recharge rate is permanently increased by 25%.

beginner.whatItIs: Rare add-on for Unbodied Flesh that feeds Headlong Flight with fresh charges every time a generator hits completion. The recharge rate also surges for a short burst after each repair, and once enough generators are done the dash locks in at full charge with a permanent boost.
beginner.whyItMatters: The charge grants land at natural pressure points in the trial, and the temporary recharge boost lets the killer chain dashes without a long flat period. The full charge on a nearly completed map locks in a late-game burst that punishes the final push.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It syncs naturally with groups that push through generators in rapid succession, since each completed machine hands back a dash charge and a short recharge spike. At rare rarity it stands out as a worthwhile slot for chase builds that lean on constant repositioning rather than raw pressure.

Addon_K41_12.name: Dulled Knife
Addon_K41_12.description:
A stage prop, symbolic of a woman's gambit in an attempt to save her lover on death's row.

Decreases Headlong Flight's charge consumption by 25%.Glowing Fungus grants Survivors 10% Haste for 5 seconds while preventing scratch marks, pools of blood, grunts of pain, and aura reveals.

Haste increases Survivor's movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Rare add-on for Unbodied Flesh that trims the charge cost of Headlong Flight so the dash stays available longer between uses. It also reshapes the Glowing Fungus: instead of a pure penalty, it now grants the survivor a brief Haste window while suppressing their scratch marks, blood trails, and aura tells.
beginner.whyItMatters: Cutting the dash cost keeps mobility constant through long chases, and the fungus flip means a survivor who eats one trades visibility and noise for a short sprint window. The net effect is a power that rewards reading the survivor's decisions rather than just applying pressure.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in lobbies where the group relies on speed and silence to escape, since the fungus now trades visibility for movement. Its rare rarity makes it a strong upgrade slot, but the survivor speed bonus means the killer must still close the gap after the boost fades.

Addon_K41_13.name: Spattered Handkerchief
Addon_K41_13.description:
A sign that something was very wrong presented itself but she chose to ignore it.

When the exit gates are powered, all Survivors are afflicted with Leeched I. Glowing Fungi begin to decay and activating Corporeal Weave no longer creates new Glowing Fungi.

beginner.whatItIs: Rare add-on for Unbodied Flesh that floods every survivor with the early Leeched tier the moment the exit gates come online. Existing Glowing Fungi start to decay, and Corporeal Weave stops producing new ones, winding the power down as the trial nears its end.
beginner.whyItMatters: Hitting every survivor with the Leeched state the instant the gates power on strips away the freedom they were saving for the final escape, while the decaying fungi and locked Corporeal Weave keep the map from flooding with new debuff zones. The net result is a late-game squeeze that shifts pressure toward the exit rather than the generators.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in lobbies where the group clings to generators and waits for the gates, since the late-game infection punishes that stalling strategy. Rare rarity makes it a meaningful pick, so build the rest of the kit to sustain pressure into the final gate phase.

Addon_K41_14.name: Framed Newspaper
Addon_K41_14.description:
She had once made it onto the entertainment section of the city's newspaper but she wanted more.

Increases Headlong Flight's charges by 6 and its recharge rate by 15%.Headlong Flight must be at least half-charged to activate.

beginner.whatItIs: An Unbodied Flesh add-on that gives Headlong Flight extra charges and a quicker recharge, so the dash comes back faster after each use. In exchange, the ability needs to reach at least half its charge before it can be triggered at all.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra charges and quicker refill turn Headlong Flight into a recurring escape tool rather than a one-shot burst, which shifts the Krasue's rhythm toward repeated speed surges instead of a single sprint. It reads as a meaningful change to the power's identity since the tool becomes far more central to her chase game.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a trial feels like it runs out of early momentum and the Krasue needs repeat dashes to close gaps on scattered survivors. Its rare rarity keeps it accessible enough to try in a speed-focused Krasue loadout without a deep collection grind.

Addon_K41_15.name: Lorenza's Remains
Addon_K41_15.description:
Even her pet bird would fall victim to the Krasue's thirst for blood.

Leeched I applies Blindness.Leeched II applies 4% Hindered.

Blindness prevents Survivors from seeing auras.

Hindered reduces Survivor movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: An Unbodied Flesh add-on that layers Blindness onto the first tier of Leeched, then adds a movement-speed penalty to the second tier. Each successive leech stage starts to close off what survivors can see and how quickly they can escape.
beginner.whyItMatters: The combination of hiding survivor auras and slowing them down turns a defensive stacking mechanic into a tool that punishes survivors for recovering, which is a bigger shift in how the power plays than a minor stat bump. It makes the Krasue's pressure more oppressive over time since each leech layer compounds into both information denial and physical slowdown.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in matchups where survivors lean on healing and information to recover, because the aura blindness disrupts their ability to coordinate while the slowdown drags out every interaction. Its very rare rarity makes it a find worth saving for a Krasue build focused on sustained pressure.

Addon_K41_16.name: Shredded Gown
Addon_K41_16.description:
She tore at her clothes and into her flesh as her body burnt.

Corporeal Weave reveals the auras of all Survivors who are within 8 meters of Glowing Fungus or holding Glowing Fungus of their own for 5 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: An Unbodied Flesh add-on that makes Corporeal Weave briefly reveal the auras of any survivor standing close to a Glowing Fungus or carrying one of their own. The reveal window is short but can pin down hidden survivors during a critical moment.
beginner.whyItMatters: Revealing survivors who are collecting or loitering around Glowing Fungus turns a single-area tool into a map-wide information source, since survivors often cluster around fungus to gain their own perks. It is a larger shift in how the power reads because it converts a defensive or area-denial tool into a tracking ability with a clear tactical read.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when survivors are spamming Glowing Fungus to gain defensive perks, since the aura reveal forces them to pick between taking the fungus risk or giving up its benefit. Its iridescent rarity makes it a standout find for Krasue players who want information control without a dedicated tracking perk.

Addon_K41_17.name: Rotten Swine
Addon_K41_17.description:
A revolting meal that left her disgusted when she awoke.

Whenever you hit a Generator, dropped Pallet, or Breakable Wall with Leeching Gland, it is marked.You damage or basic-break the marked object 15% faster, then the mark is removed.Only one object can be marked at a time.

beginner.whatItIs: Rotten Swine slots into Unbodied Flesh and marks a Generator, dropped Pallet, or Breakable Wall struck by Leeching Gland, speeding up damage and basic-breaking on that object until the mark drops. Only one object can carry the mark at a time, so choosing which target to flag is a deliberate decision.
beginner.whyItMatters: Marking and then prioritizing a specific object is a small tactical tweak layered onto an already offensive power, because it lets the Krasue focus pressure on one target instead of spreading effort across the map. The speed bonus on the marked object is modest in isolation, but it changes the feel of map control by making each hit feel more purposeful.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it when a survivor is stalling on a single generator or protecting a pallet chain, since marking the object already under attack creates a rhythm of focused pressure. Its very rare rarity means it rewards patients who build around sustained map denial.

Addon_K41_18.name: Theater Binoculars
Addon_K41_18.description:
A pair of glasses that have watched many tragedies.

Hitting a non-Leeched Survivor with Intestinal Whip reveals the auras of other Survivors within 24 meters for 5 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Theater Binoculars plugs into Unbodied Flesh so that landing Intestinal Whip on a survivor without a leech exposes the auras of other survivors nearby for a short window. A single clean strike becomes a moment of broad awareness across the immediate area.
beginner.whyItMatters: Turning a single-hit power into a tracking trigger is a meaningful change to the power's identity, because it converts a damage tool into an information play that punishes survivors who rely on hiding. The reveal window is short but reliable, which makes it feel like a tactical tool rather than a passive stat.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in trials where survivors camp near generators or windows and rely on darkness to coordinate, since the whip-triggered aura reveal breaks their information advantage. Its rare rarity keeps it within reach for a Krasue loadout that wants a tracking edge.

Addon_K41_19.name: Queen's Scepter
Addon_K41_19.description:
The stage prop of a vengeful queen who demands blood.

Successful Intestinal Whip hits cause a Leeching Gland to spatter near the Survivor.

beginner.whatItIs: Queen's Scepter pairs with Unbodied Flesh and drops a Leeching Gland near a survivor every time Intestinal Whip connects successfully. Each clean hit plants a leech on the spot, chaining strikes into growing territorial control without needing a separate trip to that area.
beginner.whyItMatters: Dropping a Leeching Gland directly on a survivor's position is a meaningful shift in the power's identity, because it extends the Krasue's pressure without a setup step. It creates a loop where a whip hit sets up the next pressure point, making the whole power feel more interconnected and harder to predict.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors are rotating through generators quickly, since the spattered Leeching Gland forces them to either stop and deal with it or risk a leech stack later. Its very rare rarity makes it a standout upgrade for Krasue builds that already revolve around Intestinal Whip timing.

Addon_K41_20.name: Mysterious Elixir
Addon_K41_20.description:
A liquid moulded from The Fog itself. Though similar to the concoction she drank, there seem to be slight alterations.

Whenever you hit a Window with Leeching Gland, it is markedWhenever you vault the marked Window, it is blocked for 10 seconds, then the mark is removed.Only one Window can be marked at a time.

beginner.whatItIs: Mysterious Elixir attaches to Unbodied Flesh and flags a Window the instant Leeching Gland strikes it. Vaulting through that flagged Window blocks it for a short stretch, and only one Window can hold the flag at a time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blocking a window after a leech hit is a noticeable change to the kill flow, because it turns a single defensive tool into a temporary lockdown that traps survivors in one direction. The mark-and-vault mechanic adds a deliberate setup step, which makes the power feel more tactical and less automatic.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in maps with tight window loops where a blocked escape route forces survivors to backtrack into the Krasue's reach. Its very rare rarity makes it a high-value find for players who build around window control and area denial.

Addon_K42_01.name: Orderly ID
Addon_K42_01.description:
Bears the face of Henry Creel as he appeared before he was changed by another dimension.

While out of Worldbreaker Mode, the Vine Attack's aiming range is increased by 2 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: Orderly ID extends the aiming range of the Vine Attack for Test Subject while the killer remains outside Worldbreaker Mode. The extra reach makes it simpler to track a moving survivor from a slightly further distance.
beginner.whyItMatters: A slightly longer aiming window is a small but useful tweak, because it gives the killer a bit more leeway to connect without needing to be perfectly aligned with the target. It does not change the power's core identity, but it makes each attempt feel a little more forgiving.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when learning the killer's Vine Attack timing feels too tight, since the extra range smooths out the aiming margin. Its common rarity makes it an easy early find for anyone starting a build around the dimension-shifting power.

Addon_K42_02.name: Bead Maze
Addon_K42_02.description:
A developmental toy used to enrich the minds of captive children.

The second phase of the Worldbreaker Timer is increased by 2.5 seconds for each living Survivor.

beginner.whatItIs: Bead Maze lengthens the second phase of the Worldbreaker Timer on Test Subject, with the bonus scaling for every living survivor still in the match. The more survivors remain, the longer that phase stretches out.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer second phase is a modest timing tweak that gives the killer slightly more time to reposition or chase during the transition between modes. The scaling to surviving players means the effect is more meaningful in lategame scenarios, which shifts the power's value toward endgame pressure.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the Worldbreaker Timer feels too fast to set up a strong position before the second phase ends. Its common rarity keeps it within reach for early-game loadouts focused on timing the mode switch.

Addon_K42_03.name: Shattered Wrist Rocket
Addon_K42_03.description:
A once-powerful slingshot, now laid to ruin.

Whenever you Undergate attack, dropped Pallets and Generators caught in the blast special-break and explode.

beginner.whatItIs: Shattered Wrist Rocket feeds the Undergate blast on Test Subject, forcing any dropped Pallet or Generator in the area to special-break and explode outright. A well-placed Undergate can wipe out a whole cluster of objectives in one press.
beginner.whyItMatters: Exploding generators and pallets on contact is a bigger shift in the zone's identity, because it turns the Undergate from a zone tool into a map-disruption event that can destroy progress outright. It changes how survivors think about where to camp, since a generator that has survived the rest of the trial can be wiped in one hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in trials where survivors cluster around generators for safe camping, since the explosion forces them to either scatter or risk losing a generator's worth of progress. Its uncommon rarity makes it a solid mid-collection find for builds that want map destruction.

Addon_K42_04.name: Stained Glass Mural
Addon_K42_04.description:
A design once found on the Creel family door. Now it darkens the door of another dimension.

While Upside Down traversal is on cooldown, whenever you basic-break Pallets or Breakable Walls, the cooldown decreases by 12 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Stained Glass Mural chews down the Upside Down traversal cooldown for Test Subject each time the killer basic-breaks a Pallet or Breakable Wall while the cooldown is still ticking. Routine basic-breaking becomes a way to pull traversal back sooner.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster traversal cooldown from breaking map objects is a modest but meaningful tweak, because it rewards active map control and keeps the killer's movement tool coming back more quickly. It shifts the feel of the power from waiting out a long cooldown to using the cooldown as an active part of the kill flow.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the Upside Down traversal cooldown feels too long between chases, since breaking a few pallets on the way to a chase can bring the tool back sooner. Its common rarity makes it an easy pick for any build that leans on traversal as a chase tool.

Addon_K42_05.name: Smashed Cassette Deck
Addon_K42_05.description:
They once used music to escape Henry's grasp. Without it, they do not stand a chance.

At the start of the match, all Survivors scream.

All Survivors start with one Worldbreaker token. When Worldbreaker is activated for the first time, all Survivors lose their Worldbreaker Tokens. 

1 less Grandfather Clock appears on the map.

beginner.whatItIs: Smashed Cassette Deck reshapes how Test Subject begins: every survivor screams at the trial's opening and carries a Worldbreaker token into the match. Those tokens vanish the instant Worldbreaker first activates, and the map spawns with fewer Grandfather Clocks than usual.
beginner.whyItMatters: The opening scream is a larger shift in the power's identity, because it immediately disrupts survivor coordination and forces early decisions without the killer having to chase anyone. The reduced Grandfather Clock count also shrinks the survivors' tool pool, which compounds the early pressure into a sustained advantage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in trials against coordinated survivor teams that rely on early calm to set up their strategy, since the forced scream breaks that rhythm. Its uncommon rarity makes it a solid find for builds that want to set the tone from the first few seconds.

Addon_K42_06.name: Bloody Roller Skate
Addon_K42_06.description:
A memento of the fury that Eleven was capable of.

When activating the Undergate Attack, the Killer gains a 20% Haste status effect for 1.5 seconds upon exiting.

Haste increases Killer movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Bloody Roller Skate grants a brief Haste boost to Test Subject the instant the Undergate attack ends. The speed surge lasts only a moment, but it is enough to lunge toward the next target rather than standing still after the zone clears.
beginner.whyItMatters: Closing distance immediately after a zone attack keeps the pressure on and removes the beat where survivors can slip away. It reads as a modest quality-of-life improvement to the Undergate rhythm rather than a fundamental shift in how the power functions.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when exiting the Undergate attack often leaves the killer too far from the next target, since the burst bridges that gap for a beat. Its uncommon rarity makes it an easy upgrade for any build that uses the Undergate as a setup tool.

Addon_K42_07.name: Gutted Supercom
Addon_K42_07.description:
A broken communication device that now crackles to life at the most terrifying times.

While out of Worldbreaker Mode, Survivors hit by Vine Attacks have their aura shown for 1.5 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Gutted Supercom briefly exposes the aura of any survivor struck by a Vine Attack while Test Subject is outside Worldbreaker Mode. The reveal anchors tracking to the standard hunting phase rather than the transformation.
beginner.whyItMatters: A short aura reveal on hit is a small information tweak, because it gives the killer a moment of positional clarity in a power that otherwise relies on blind aim. It does not change the power's core loop, but it reduces the frustration of missing and losing the thread of a chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the Vine Attack feels like it hits and then the killer loses track of where the survivor went, since the brief aura window keeps the chase connected. Its uncommon rarity makes it a reasonable find for any build that leans on Vine Attack accuracy.

Addon_K42_08.name: Mid-Century Radio
Addon_K42_08.description:
It sat silent in the Creel's dining room until the slaughter was about to begin.

While in Worldbreaker Mode, Grandfather Clocks more than 32 meters away being worked on by Survivors have their auras revealed.

beginner.whatItIs: Mid-Century Radio reveals the auras of Grandfather Clocks being worked on by survivors far from the killer, but only during Test Subject's Worldbreaker Mode. It stretches awareness well beyond the immediate area without needing a chase in progress.
beginner.whyItMatters: Revealing distant Grandfather Clocks in Worldbreaker Mode is a meaningful change to the tracking game, because it lets the killer see where survivors are completing the mode's key interactions without being physically nearby. It extends the power's tracking value into a map-wide read during the most important phase of the match.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when survivors are spread out and completing Grandfather Clocks in corners of the map, since the aura reveal helps the killer anticipate where the next Worldbreaker activation will come from. Its common rarity makes it an easy find for any build that wants better information in Worldbreaker Mode.

Addon_K42_09.name: Clock Hands
Addon_K42_09.description:
Hands of the Creel family's grandfather clock, corrupted by Henry's dark power.

Survivors gain the Oblivious status effect when interacting with Grandfather Clocks, and for 12 seconds after.

Oblivious prevents Survivors from hearing or being affected by the Killer's Terror Radius.

beginner.whatItIs: Clock Hands slots into the test subject power and renders survivors Oblivious when they interact with a Grandfather Clock. While Oblivious, they cannot hear or be affected by the killer's Terror Radius. The effect lingers briefly after the interaction ends, blinding them to the killer's presence as they run.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing Terror Radius awareness during and after a Grandfather Clock interaction is a full stealth shift in the power's feel, because it blinds survivors to the killer's approach at exactly the moment they are most vulnerable. It turns the Grandfather Clock interaction from a safe, focused task into a risk that can be punished immediately after.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in trials where survivors lean heavily on Grandfather Clock downtime to reposition safely, since the Oblivious window strips their ability to feel the killer nearby. Its uncommon drop rate keeps it accessible enough to slot in without crowding out other options.

Addon_K42_10.name: Electrode Cap
Addon_K42_10.description:
Used to measure the brain's electrical activity. In the lab, nothing goes unnoticed.

At the start of the second phase of Worldbreaker Mode (or when Survivors complete the Grandfather Clock interactions), Survivors more than 26 meters away from the Killer have their aura revealed for 6 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Electrode Cap attaches to the Entity's test subject power and flares the auras of far-flung survivors the instant Worldbreaker Mode shifts into its second phase. The same reveal fires when survivors finish their Grandfather Clock interactions. Either trigger strips concealment and forces hidden survivors into the open.
beginner.whyItMatters: Surfacing far-away positions right as Worldbreaker Mode escalates gives the killer a clear read on where everyone is heading. Because the reveal can also fire every time survivors finish a Grandfather Clock interaction, it can hand over more than a single positional spike across that phase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the second phase of Worldbreaker Mode starts and the killer needs to find scattered survivors quickly, since the reveal window points directly at where they are hiding. Its rare rarity makes it a worthwhile find for builds that want a one-shot information spike at a key moment.

Addon_K42_11.name: Forged Death Certificate
Addon_K42_11.description:
A piece of paper used to prove the death of a powerful person who was very much alive.

Whenever you successfully place a Worldbreaker Token on a Survivor via Vine Attack, you gain Undetectable Status Effect until the next Worldbreaker Mode activation.

Undetectable hides the Killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain.

beginner.whatItIs: Forged Death Certificate plugs into the test subject power and wraps the killer in Undetectable the moment a Worldbreaker Token lands on a survivor through a Vine Attack. The concealment masks aura, Terror Radius, and red stain all at once. It holds until the next Worldbreaker Mode activation, giving the killer a long window of stealth.
beginner.whyItMatters: Becoming undetectable after a successful token placement is a bigger shift in the stealth game, because it removes the killer's aura, Terror Radius, and red stain for the entire duration, which is a full invisibility window. It converts a single successful hit into a sustained stealth advantage that reshapes how survivors track the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in trials where Vine Attack hits land consistently, since each successful token placement unlocks a full stealth window that resets only on the next mode activation. Its rare drop rate makes it a premium find worth building around when the killer can maintain that hit accuracy.

Addon_K42_12.name: Rabbit Remains
Addon_K42_12.description:
Before massacring his family, Henry started small, killing rabbits and leaving their corpses strewn about town.

Survivors gain the Exhausted status effect when standing in or entering the Undergate's attack radius, and for 10 seconds after.

Increases the cooldown of Upside Down traversal by 5 seconds

Exhausted prevents Survivors from activating certain perks.

beginner.whatItIs: Rabbit Remains slots into Henry's test subject power and drains survivors who linger inside the Undergate attack radius. The Exhausted status saps their ability to activate certain perks and lingers for a short time after they leave the zone. It also lengthens the recovery time before Upside Down traversal can be used again, compounding the penalty around the area.
beginner.whyItMatters: Exhausting survivors in the Undergate zone is a meaningful change to the zone's purpose, because it disables their perks and punishes them for lingering where they think they are safe. The increased traversal cooldown is a trade-off that makes the tool less available, but the exhaustion effect is strong enough to justify that cost in most matchups.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors camp inside the Undergate after a chase, since the Exhausted window strips their perk activation and forces them out of the defensive pocket. Its very rare drop rate makes it a prized find that rewards builds willing to commit to the Undergate as a primary tool.

Addon_K42_13.name: Neck Tendril
Addon_K42_13.description:
He was furious when the tendril was torn from his neck as Max escaped his mind realm.

Survivors hit by the Vine Attack while in Worldbreaker Mode receive Hemorrhage and Mangled status effects for 70 seconds.

Hemorrhage regresses healing progress when not healing, and increases blood trails left by injured Survivors. This lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

Mangled increases time required to heal by 25% and lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Neck Tendril bolts onto the test subject power and pummels any survivor struck by the Vine Attack during Worldbreaker Mode with both Hemorrhage and Mangled. Hemorrhage bleeds off healing progress and thickens the blood trail left behind. Mangled stretches the time needed to finish a heal, turning a quick top-up into a drawn-out ordeal.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stacking two negative status effects on a single Vine Attack hit is a bigger shift in the debuff game, because Hemorrhage bleeds healing progress and Mangled slows the healing speed, which together make the survivor's recovery window feel much longer. It turns a single hit in Worldbreaker Mode into a sustained debuff that compounds over time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a team leans on quick heals to recover from chase injuries, because the paired debuffs drag out every recovery and force survivors to stay safe far longer. It drops at a rare rate, so hold the slot for trials where healing should feel punishingly slow.

Addon_K42_14.name: Victor's Razor Blade
Addon_K42_14.description:
In his grief, Henry's father used a hidden blade to take out his own eyes.

When Worldbreaker Mode ends, injured Survivors become afflicted with the Broken status effect for the next 20 seconds.

Broken prevents Survivors from being healed.

beginner.whatItIs: A rare modifier for Worldbreaker that marks injured survivors with the Broken status the moment the mode ends. While Broken, a survivor cannot be healed for a short window, which extends the killer's advantage after the mode drops.
beginner.whyItMatters: A survivor who took a hit during Worldbreaker Mode cannot be patched up in the seconds after it fades, leaving them exposed while the killer closes in or sets up the next hook. The effect is brief but lands at a moment when survivors are most likely to assume they are safe.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want to punish survivors who were injured right before Worldbreaker Mode ends, since the Broken window overlaps with their natural recovery. It is a rare drop, so it will not appear in every trial.

Addon_K42_15.name: Broken Skateboard
Addon_K42_15.description:
A cool way to get around, smashed by a furious brother as a means of control.

When Worldbreaker Mode starts, you basic-vault Windows 30% faster and auras of Pallets and Windows are revealed to you within 32 meters for the next 65 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: A very rare upgrade for Worldbreaker that kicks in the moment the mode begins. It speeds up basic window vaulting and lights up nearby pallet and window auras for a stretched-out period while the mode runs.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster vaulting keeps the killer moving through tight survivor loops without losing momentum, and the aura reveal helps track where survivors are stalling before the next chase. Together these make Worldbreaker Mode feel more mobile and information-rich.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a map has lots of windows in common chase routes, since the vault speed bonus and aura reveal combine to make those corridors dangerous for survivors trying to loop. Being very rare, expect to wait between trials before finding one.

Addon_K42_16.name: Black Widow Spider
Addon_K42_16.description:
A terrifying spider that is no longer a mere hallucination.

Entering the Upside Down while in Worldbreaker Mode makes the furthest Survivor, more than 36 meters away reveal their location for 3 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: A very rare Worldbreaker modifier that fires when the killer drops into the Upside Down during an active mode. It briefly exposes the position of whichever survivor is farthest away from the killer at that moment.
beginner.whyItMatters: That burst of information lets the killer redirect a chase toward a survivor who is far ahead, turning a moment of invisibility into a tactical reposition. It is a small but decisive information tool that requires no extra input beyond the action already being taken.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the Worldbreaker build already uses the Upside Down frequently, since the aura reveal triggers on the same action that is part of the rotation. It is a very rare drop, so plan around it rather than expecting it every trial.

Addon_K42_17.name: Pizza Goggles
Addon_K42_17.description:
Used while Eleven entered sensory deprivation, they rid the user of distractions and focus the mind.

The Undergate Attack's area of effect range is reduced by 90%, and its cooldown time is shortened by 25 seconds.

Your exit cooldown time after executing the Undergate Attack is reduced by 80%.

beginner.whatItIs: Rare modifier for the Test Subject power that tightens the Undergate Attack hit zone to a narrow radius. The trade-off is worth it: both the recovery timer and the post-attack exit delay shrink, letting the killer land the strike again much sooner.
beginner.whyItMatters: The smaller hit area means the Undergate Attack is less forgiving to aim, but the much faster cooldown means it is available far more often in a chase. The reduced exit cooldown also lets the killer reposition and re-engage almost immediately after landing the hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if the Worldbreaker build already chains Undergate Attacks into the chase, since the faster cooldown more than makes up for the tighter hit zone. It is a rare drop.

Addon_K42_18.name: Electroshock Collar
Addon_K42_18.description:
A cruelly efficient method of training and punishing the facility's prisoners.

When coming out of the Upside Down, for 12 seconds, all Windows within 32 meters are blocked.

beginner.whatItIs: Electroshock Collar is a very rare modifier attached to the Test Subject power. The moment the killer surfaces from the Upside Down, every window in the surrounding area locks shut, denying survivors any vault escape for a short period.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blocked windows force survivors to detour, which can break a chase loop or strand a survivor in an open area. The effect lands exactly when the killer is re-emerging and re-engaging, making it a natural interrupt on survivor escape routes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when facing a survivor who relies on window vaults to escape, since the blocked windows create a momentary wall at the exact spot the killer is standing. It is a very rare drop.

Addon_K42_19.name: Chess Piece
Addon_K42_19.description:
One of the few forms of entertainment while in the facility, it helped the students learn logic and tactics.

The Vine Attack has two charges, and its attack radius is diminished by 40%.

beginner.whatItIs: An iridescent modifier for Worldbreaker that grants the Vine Attack an extra charge while trimming its strike radius. The trade favors frequency over reach, letting the killer string together more vine hits in a tighter space.
beginner.whyItMatters: Having an extra charge means the killer can land a Vine Attack, reposition, and land another one without waiting for a full cooldown. The smaller radius is a fair trade, since the second use extends the window of pressure on a survivor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a chase keeps looping the same corridor and the extra Vine Attack lets the killer re-engage without waiting for a full reset. It drops at iridescent rarity.

Addon_K42_20.name: Iridescent Soteria Chip
Addon_K42_20.description:
A chip that once limited his powers is now a source of even greater power.

When Worldbreaker activates, the Killer gains Undetectable, and Survivors with at least one Worldbreaker Token have their aura revealed when coming within 12 meters of the Killer.

This lasts until the Killer performs a Vine Attack, enters the Upside Down, or Worldbreaker ends.

Undetectable hides the Killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain.

beginner.whatItIs: An iridescent modifier for Worldbreaker that wraps the killer in Undetectable the moment the mode kicks in. Any survivor carrying a Worldbreaker Token will have their aura exposed if they drift close, and the stealth holds until the killer fires a Vine Attack, enters the Upside Down, or the mode expires.
beginner.whyItMatters: Hiding the killer's aura, terror radius, and red stain forces survivors to guess where the killer is, while the token-based reveal punishes survivors who have been marked by Worldbreaker. The two effects work together to invert the information balance during the mode.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want Worldbreaker Mode to be a cat-and-mouse phase where the killer stays hidden while token-marked survivors are tracked down. It is an iridescent drop.

Addon_K43_01.name: Garden Claw
Addon_K43_01.description:
Good for digging up weeds and digging into human flesh.

Increases the duration of Killer Instinct after a Jump Scare by 2 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Common modifier for Omnipresent Evil that extends how long Killer Instinct persists after a Jump Scare lands. That extra detection time widens the hunt window and makes it harder for the struck survivor to slip away.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer Killer Instinct window gives the killer more time to lock onto a survivor's location after a successful scare, making it easier to re-engage before they find cover. The extension is modest but reliable across every scare.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you tend to lose track of survivors right after a Jump Scare, since the extra Killer Instinct time bridges that gap. Being a common drop, it should appear frequently enough to be a solid default.

Addon_K43_02.name: Bent Wheel
Addon_K43_02.description:
All that remained of the victim's wheelchair after the fatal blow.

Increases the range at which you can trigger Jump Scare by 4 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: Common modifier for Omnipresent Evil that pushes the Jump Scare activation range outward. The killer can scare from farther away, compressing the reaction window a survivor has before the hit connects.
beginner.whyItMatters: A wider scare radius means the killer can catch survivors off guard from slightly further away, turning a near-miss into a successful Jump Scare. This small extension matters most in tight indoor sections where distance margins are thin.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you find yourself narrowly missing Jump Scare triggers in close-quarters areas, since the extra range closes that gap. It is a common drop.

Addon_K43_03.name: Knitting Needle
Addon_K43_03.description:
You won't believe what—and who—this thing has been through.

Increases the time it takes for injured Impaled Survivors to extract the Spike from themselves by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Common modifier for Omnipresent Evil that stretches out how long an injured survivor takes to remove the Spike. The prolonged struggle keeps them pinned in place and makes escaping noticeably harder.
beginner.whyItMatters: A slower extraction means a survivor spends more time pinned to the ground after being spiked, which gives the killer a longer window to re-engage or hook them. It punishes the natural recovery rhythm of the Impaled state.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want to extend the punishment phase of a spike, especially against survivors who normally recover quickly. It is a common drop.

Addon_K43_04.name: Orderly's Shoe
Addon_K43_04.description:
It hung from her twitching foot as the knife plunged into her belly.

Increases the duration of Haste after a Jump Scare by 5 seconds.

Haste increases Killer movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Orderly's Shoe is a common modifier for Omnipresent Evil that stretches the Haste window earned from a Jump Scare. The longer speed window keeps pressure on survivors who are scrambling to vault or lose the killer's line of sight.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extended Haste window means the killer maintains that speed advantage well past the scare, closing the gap on a survivor who vaults into a tight loop. It rewards clean aggression by keeping the momentum rolling when the chase matters most.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if the playstyle is built around landing Jump Scares and then immediately chasing, since the extended Haste makes that follow-up pursuit smoother. It is a common drop.

Addon_K43_05.name: Sleeping Bag
Addon_K43_05.description:
An absolutely awful place to hide from a killer.

After grabbing a Hook Spike while in Omnipresent Evil mode, see the locations of Survivors within 10 meters of hooks.

beginner.whatItIs: An uncommon Omnipresent Evil modifier that reveals nearby survivor positions after the killer collects a Hook Spike. It pins down who is lurking around the hooks, making it harder for a survivor to hide in plain sight.
beginner.whyItMatters: That brief aura window lets the killer see which survivors are clustering around hooks, which is useful information when deciding whether to reposition or continue the chase. It turns the spike-grab action into a scouting tool at no extra cost.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want to read the hook area before committing to the next move, since the reveal triggers automatically when the spike is grabbed. It is an uncommon drop.

Addon_K43_06.name: Bloody Smile
Addon_K43_06.description:
He wasn't happy after his face was smashed into a tree.

Increases Jump Scare and Omnipresent Evil's detection range of Survivors by 4 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: Uncommon modifier for Omnipresent Evil that extends both the Jump Scare trigger range and the power's survivor detection reach. The killer spots and strikes from farther away, catching survivors who thought they were still out of reach.
beginner.whyItMatters: A wider detection radius means the killer can sense and scare survivors from a greater distance, reducing the chances of a survivor slipping past unnoticed. The effect applies to both the scare and the sensing ability, so the two bonuses compound on each other.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want a wider safety net on survivor detection, since the extra range on both Jump Scare and Omnipresent Evil sensing reduces the chance of a survivor going undetected. It is an uncommon drop.

Addon_K43_07.name: Toxic Waste
Addon_K43_07.description:
No one could survive being submerged in this poison.

After a Jump Scare, Survivors within 10 meters of a hook or Scrap Pile gain Oblivious for 13 seconds.

Oblivious prevents Survivors from hearing and being affected by the Killer's Terror Radius.

beginner.whatItIs: Uncommon modifier for Omnipresent Evil that drops Oblivious on any survivor positioned near a hook or scrap pile after a Jump Scare connects. Affected targets lose all Terror Radius awareness for a meaningful stretch, dulling their spatial sense.
beginner.whyItMatters: Oblivious removes a survivor's ability to hear the killer's approach, which is a significant loss of information for them. Survivors near hooks are often in the middle of a recovery action, so the timing lands when they are most exposed to a re-engage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want to blind survivors who are clustered around hooks after a scare, since the Oblivious window overlaps with their natural recovery time. It is an uncommon drop.

Addon_K43_08.name: Party Noisemaker
Addon_K43_08.description:
A party instument that tore through a woman's eyeball and gouged her brain.

Breaking a Pallet or Breakable Wall with Jump Scare reveals the Auras of Survivors further than 28 meters for 6 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Uncommon modifier for Omnipresent Evil that triggers a wide aura reveal whenever a Jump Scare shatters a pallet or breakable wall. Distant survivors flash visibly to the killer for a brief moment, letting the strike double as a tracking tool.
beginner.whyItMatters: Breaking a pallet during a Jump Scare already signals that the killer is present, and adding a distant aura reveal on top of that gives the killer a clear line of sight to survivors farther away. It turns a defensive survivor action into an information leak for the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want every pallet break during a Jump Scare to also flush out a distant survivor, since the reveal triggers on the same action. It is an uncommon drop.

Addon_K43_09.name: Coroner's Coffee
Addon_K43_09.description:
A cup of coffee that went unfinished.

Increases the distance Survivors are pushed by Spikes by 25%.

Gain 13% Haste for 3 seconds after injuring a Survivor with a Spike if they do not collide with the environment.

Haste increases Killer movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Coroner's Coffee is an uncommon modifier for Omnipresent Evil that pushes survivors farther on a Spike hit and rewards the killer with a brief Haste burst. The speed bonus only triggers when the struck survivor does not slam into a wall or object.
beginner.whyItMatters: A stronger spike push creates more space between the killer and the survivor, making it harder for them to immediately loop back into cover. The Haste reward for a clean hit with no wall collision gives the killer a speed boost to maintain pressure after the spike lands.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want spikes to create more separation and reward clean hits with a speed boost, since both effects stack on the same spike interaction. It is an uncommon drop.

Addon_K43_10.name: Sauna Rock
Addon_K43_10.description:
Nicely weighted, could be used to crush a rib cage.

After a Jump Scare, inflict all Survivors within Killer Instinct's detection range with Exhausted for 3 seconds.

Exhausted prevents Survivors from activating exhausting perks.

beginner.whatItIs: Rare modifier for Omnipresent Evil that inflicts Exhausted on every survivor within Killer Instinct range after a Jump Scare lands. The debuff locks out any perk that normally spends exhaustion to activate, robbing the affected survivor of those escape options.
beginner.whyItMatters: Exhausted prevents survivors from using their exhausting perks, which removes a key defensive tool during the moments right after a scare. Hitting every survivor in the Killer Instinct zone makes this a broad crowd-control effect rather than a single-target one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want to shut down survivor perks in a cluster after a scare, since the Exhausted effect hits everyone in range at once. It is a rare drop.

Addon_K43_11.name: Mirror Shards
Addon_K43_11.description:
A weapon that dealt more than bad luck.

Impaled Survivors become Broken for 40 seconds after extracting the Spike.

Broken prevents Survivors from being healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Rare modifier for Omnipresent Evil that marks an impaled survivor as Broken the instant the Spike is extracted. While Broken, the survivor cannot be healed by anyone, pinning the injury in place for the full duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: Broken prevents healing, so a survivor who has just freed themselves from a spike cannot be patched up for a long stretch afterward. This extends the effective punishment of a spike well beyond the moment of extraction.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want the spike's consequence to linger, especially when a teammate is nearby and a quick heal would otherwise restore the survivor to fighting condition. It is a rare drop.

Addon_K43_12.name: Imprinted Aluminum
Addon_K43_12.description:
It's either avant-garde artwork, or the horrified imprint of a woman whose face was slammed into it.

Injuring a healthy Survivor with a Spike inflicts the Mangled and Hemorrhage status effects for 70 seconds.

Mangled increases time required to heal by 25% and lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

Hemorrhage regresses healing progress when not healing, and increases blood trails left by injured survivors. This lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Imprinted Aluminum is a rare upgrade for Omnipresent Evil that stamps Mangled and Hemorrhage onto a healthy survivor the moment a Spike lands. Mangled stretches out the time needed to be healed, while Hemorrhage bleeds healing progress away and thickens the blood trail a wounded survivor leaves behind.
beginner.whyItMatters: Mangled slows healing and Hemorrhage causes healing progress to regress, so a healthy survivor who gets spiked faces a much harder road to full recovery. The combination makes the spike a genuine threat even to a survivor who was not yet injured.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want spikes to be dangerous even against healthy survivors, since the dual status effects turn a single spike into a prolonged debuff. It is a rare drop.

Addon_K43_13.name: Two Nails
Addon_K43_13.description:
A reliable way to hold a corpse's wrist in place.

Spikes that come within 1 meter of a Survivor reveal their Aura for 5 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Two Nails is a rare attachment for Omnipresent Evil that turns each Spike into a short-range sensor on the killer side. When a survivor drifts within close reach of one, their aura flashes briefly, stripping away the cover a stealth-focused build depends on.
beginner.whyItMatters: A spike that normally sits in a corner of the map becomes a passive sensor, flagging survivors who wander too close to its position. This is useful for tracking a survivor's path without actively chasing them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you want spikes to act as passive trackers, since the aura reveal triggers automatically when a survivor gets close. It is a rare drop.

Addon_K43_14.name: Eye Goop
Addon_K43_14.description:
What remains when a harpoon is shoved into one's eye.

Gain Undetectable for 13 seconds after grabbing a Hook Spike.

Undetectable hides the Killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain.

beginner.whatItIs: Eye Goop slots into Omnipresent Evil and grants Undetectable for a short window after grabbing a Hook Spike. During that window the killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain all vanish from survivor vision.
beginner.whyItMatters: Disappearing right after impaling a survivor removes the immediate threat of being found and freed, turning that vulnerable moment into an opportunity to reposition or chase elsewhere. It is a moderate shift in play since it changes how the killer uses the space around hooked survivors.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in chases where the killer frequently impales and wants to punish survivors who rotate to free a hooked teammate, since it breaks their coordination. It drops at a rare tier, so expect it to show up less often than common add-ons.

Addon_K43_15.name: Bloody Magazine
Addon_K43_15.description:
The spattering of blood told the story of a brutal massacre.

When a Hook Spike misses, all Survivors within 8 meters of the impact scream and reveal their Auras for 3 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: When a Hook Spike misses its target under Omnipresent Evil, Bloody Magazine forces nearby survivors to scream and flash their auras to the killer. The brief exposure opens a window to track down anyone hiding close to the impact point.
beginner.whyItMatters: A missed spike no longer goes to waste, since the reveal rewards the killer even on a whiff and can turn a failed attack into a setup for the next one. It is a small tactical tweak that adds a safety net without changing the core loop.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if misses on Hook Spikes are common, since it converts those failures into information instead of a free second for survivors. It sits at a very rare tier, so it will not appear in most unlock rotations.

Addon_K43_16.name: Burnt Fuse
Addon_K43_16.description:
The surge of electricity was overwhelming. It left the man's flesh charred and smelling of cooked meat.

While a Survivor is Impaled and for 5 seconds after they extract the Spike, the Exit Gates are blocked for them and any Survivors within 13 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: Burnt Fuse modifies Omnipresent Evil so that the Exit Gates lock out an impaled survivor and any teammate standing close to them. The block persists while the spike remains lodged and continues for a brief moment after the survivor pulls it free.
beginner.whyItMatters: Forcing survivors to fight over the spike instead of walking to the exit changes the tempo of the late game, since the killer controls whether the trial can end. It is a bigger shift because it removes the escape safety valve that survivors normally rely on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer is playing a long, controlled game and wants to force an endgame scrum, since it punishes survivors who try to free a hooked teammate and leave. It is very rare, so treat it as a special-occasion add-on rather than a default.

Addon_K43_17.name: Missing Corkscrew
Addon_K43_17.description:
It seems to always be missing when you need it on-hand.

Impaled Survivors emit a 32 meter Terror Radius until the Spike is extracted.

Gain Undetectable from the time a Survivor is Impaled to 13 seconds after they extract the Spike.

Undetectable hides the Killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain.

beginner.whatItIs: Missing Corkscrew pairs a wide Terror Radius around impaled survivors with Undetectable protection for the killer under Omnipresent Evil. The concealment lasts from the moment of impalement all the way until a short period after the survivor extracts the spike.
beginner.whyItMatters: The combination of a huge tell on the survivor and an invisible killer creates a powerful information asymmetry, since survivors cannot track where to go to free their teammate while the impaled one is glowing brightly. It is a bigger shift because it flips the usual risk-reward of freeing a hook.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the goal is to make freeing a hooked teammate feel dangerous and disorienting for the survivor team, since the killer disappears exactly when they need to find it. It is very rare, so plan builds around it deliberately rather than relying on luck to surface it.

Addon_K43_18.name: Deputy's Badge
Addon_K43_18.description:
The badge of an officer who discovered that some things aren't worth investigating.

While in Omnipresent Evil, passing within 2 meters of a generator will cause it to explode, losing 5% progress and begin regressing. If any survivors are repairing the generator, it doesn't explode, but they get a special Skill Check.

beginner.whatItIs: Deputy's Badge turns a casual walk past a generator under Omnipresent Evil into a threat. The generator detonates, losing progress and beginning to regress, unless survivors are actively repairing it, in which case they face a punishing skill check instead.
beginner.whyItMatters: Adding an explosive threat to generator space changes how survivors approach repairs, since walking near a generator now carries a real risk of losing progress. It is a moderate shift that adds a passive zoning element without requiring any direct action.
