Exposed survivors will be downed by basic attacks even if uninjured.

beginner.whatItIs: Fragrant Tuft of Hair reshapes Evil Incarnate mode for the Stalker: every survivor becomes Exposed, Lunge reaches noticeably farther, and a basic attack can down an Exposed survivor even without prior injury. The uncommon add-on swaps Slaughtering Strike out of reach in exchange for constant pressure and far easier takedowns.
beginner.whyItMatters: Losing Slaughtering Strike removes a core tool, but exposing survivors to basic-attack downs turns every encounter into a high-stakes moment. The boosted Lunge range compensates for the lost strike by making it easier to close distance and land a hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a build wants to trade the guaranteed down of Slaughtering Strike for a more aggressive, expose-and-chase game plan. The uncommon rarity makes it a meaningful commitment that suits setups built around Lunge pressure.

Addon_Stalker_GlassFragment.name: Glass Fragment
Addon_Stalker_GlassFragment.description:
A tiny piece of tinted glass, probably from a broken object. It is impossible to determine its origin.

Increases the movement speed of Slaughtering Strike by 5%.Decreases the charge speed of Slaughtering Strike by 10%.

beginner.whatItIs: Glass Fragment is a tiny sliver of tinted glass for Evil Within that speeds up Slaughtering Strike's movement while slowing its charge. The uncommon add-on trades charge speed for a faster dash once the strike is ready.
beginner.whyItMatters: The faster movement means a committed Slaughtering Strike is harder to evade once it starts, but the slower charge means there is a longer window for survivors to reposition or break line of sight. It is a speed-versus-readiness trade that rewards a killer who can sell the strike convincingly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a killer wants Slaughtering Strike to be a decisive, hard-to-avoid commitment rather than a quick, easily dodged lunge. The uncommon rarity keeps it within reach for a setup that already builds around the strike.

Addon_Stalker_HairBow.name: Hair Bow
Addon_Stalker_HairBow.description:
A blue tartan ribbon used to tie hair.

Increases the duration of Evil Incarnate by 20 seconds.Decreases the Stalk Meter fill rate by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: It slots into Evil Within and stretches the duration of Evil Incarnate. At the same time it slows the Stalk Meter fill rate, so the final phase lasts longer but takes more effort to reach.
beginner.whyItMatters: The longer final phase lets the killer apply more continuous pressure on survivors. The slower meter means more time spent in the stalking phase, a small trade-off that stretches the kill out and rewards patience.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the lobby tends to keep survivors clustered together, since a longer Evil Incarnate rewards catching several targets in one sweep. It is a rare drop, so expect to wait a few trials before it shows up.

Addon_Stalker_HairBrush.name: Hair Brush
Addon_Stalker_HairBrush.description:
A nylon bristle brush used to add body and softness to hair.

When Evil Incarnate activates, the next pallet break is 50% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Hair Brush makes the very next pallet the killer smashes break apart much faster right after Evil Incarnate begins, though only that first pallet gets the boost. The speed-up applies to breaking the pallet, not to how quickly a survivor can vault over it.
beginner.whyItMatters: That one-shot speed bonus is a small but reliable tool for pushing through dense pallet areas during the final phase. It shaves a noticeable chunk off the time it takes to clear an obstacle, which can be the difference between a clean chase and a lost one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing against survivors who lean heavily on pallet loops, since the faster break punishes them the instant they try to vault. It is uncommon, so it will appear fairly often in a normal rotation.

Addon_Stalker_Jewelry.name: Jewelry
Addon_Stalker_Jewelry.description:
A large necklace made of beads and inexpensive metals. One of Judith's favorites.

Increases the Stalk Meter fill rate on stationary Survivors by 10%.

beginner.whatItIs: A beaded necklace that accelerates Stalk Meter gain specifically against survivors who stand still. The bonus only applies when a target is not moving, so it rewards punishing hesitation.
beginner.whyItMatters: The nudge is small but targeted. Any survivor who freezes to interact with a generator or a door builds meter a little faster, which turns their moment of safety into a ticking clock for the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the lobby favors survivors who camp behind generators, since the stationary bonus punishes that playstyle directly. It is uncommon and will show up with reasonable frequency.

Addon_Stalker_JewelryBox.name: Jewelry Box
Addon_Stalker_JewelryBox.description:
A barren wooden box in which vanity items were once stored.

Increases the Stalk Meter fill rate by 30%.Decreases stalk range by 16 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: A barren wooden box that raises overall Stalk Meter fill while trimming the stalking range. The gain in fill speed is broad and applies to all targets, but the range cut is a real cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: The trade-off is bigger than most: the killer builds meter quicker but must stay closer to the target. This changes how distances are managed during stalking and suits a playstyle that already plays close.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the map is dense with cover and the killer already plays close, since the shorter range is less punishing in tight spaces. It is a rare drop.

Addon_Stalker_JMyersMemorial.name: J.Myers Memorial
Addon_Stalker_JMyersMemorial.description:
A glossy page ripped from the '65 Haddonfield High School yearbook, one dedicated to the memory of Judith Myers.

Increases pickup and hook speeds by 40% in Evil Incarnate Mode.

beginner.whatItIs: It plugs into Evil Within and boosts both pickup and hook speeds while Evil Incarnate is active. The effect applies throughout the entire final phase rather than for a short timed window.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster body handling turns the final phase into a more aggressive loop. The killer can chain hooks and reposition with less downtime, which makes the endgame feel snappier and more punishing for survivors who rely on hook placement to escape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the map layout forces survivors onto a small number of hooks, because the speed bonus makes the hook cycle feel tighter. It is a rare drop.

Addon_Stalker_JudithsJournal.name: Judith's Journal
Addon_Stalker_JudithsJournal.description:
A journal identified as owned by Judith M. Myers. Most of the pages are defaced with frightening and disturbing drawings.

Increases the Stalk Meter fill rate on the Obsession by 40%.

beginner.whatItIs: A defaced journal that sharply increases Stalk Meter gain against the current Obsession. The bonus is concentrated on a single target, making it a focused chase tool rather than a broad meter boost.
beginner.whyItMatters: A single target gaining meter noticeably faster means the final phase arrives quicker if the killer commits to one survivor. This makes a dedicated chase build far more efficient and rewards consistent focus.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer already has a clear favorite to chase and can keep eyes on one target for long stretches. It is a rare drop.

Addon_Stalker_JudithsTombstone.name: Judith's Tombstone
Addon_Stalker_JudithsTombstone.description:
A large and heavy granite tombstone stolen from Mt. Sinclair cemetery, belonging to Judith Myers.

Hooking a Survivor during Evil Incarnate refreshes its duration.Limits the duration of Evil Incarnate to 40 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: The granite tombstone refreshes Evil Incarnate the moment a hook lands, at the cost of capping the phase at a fixed maximum duration. Every successful hook resets the clock, creating a rhythm of hooks and cooldowns.
beginner.whyItMatters: The refresh mechanic turns every successful hook into a reset, which rewards aggressive body management. The cap keeps the phase from stretching indefinitely, so the killer must keep hooking to maintain pressure, a bigger shift than a simple duration bonus.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer has strong hook placement on the chosen map and can convert chases into hooks reliably. It is iridescent and will be the hardest drop to obtain in this set.

Addon_Stalker_LockOfHair.name: Lock of Hair
Addon_Stalker_LockOfHair.description:
A cut lock of blond hair bunched with a black elastic.

While Evil Incarnate is active, hold the Ability button to end it prematurely and retain 50% of the remaining duration as Stalk progress.

beginner.whatItIs: The cut lock of blond hair adds a manual exit from Evil Incarnate. Holding the ability button ends the phase early and converts some of the remaining time into Stalk Meter progress, so the next activation starts with a head start.
beginner.whyItMatters: The ability to bail out of the final phase removes the lock-in that normally forces the killer to stay exposed. The meter carry-over means the next cycle begins further along, a meaningful quality-of-life shift for a power that can feel punishing when it locks you in.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the lobby is full of survivors who use the chaos of Evil Incarnate to scatter, since the early-exit option lets the killer retreat and re-stalk instead of being stuck. It is very rare.

Addon_Stalker_MemorialFlower.name: Memorial Flower
Addon_Stalker_MemorialFlower.description:
A partially faded and dried pink larkspur picked up from a gravestone.

Increases movement speed in Stalker Mode to 4.4 m/s.

beginner.whatItIs: The dried larkspur raises the killer's movement speed while in Stalker Mode. The boost is modest but steady, applying for the entire duration of the stalking phase.
beginner.whyItMatters: A modest speed bump makes the stalking phase feel more responsive. Closing gaps with survivors a little sooner makes it easier to maintain pressure without committing to a full chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the map is open and the killer needs to cover ground quickly between generators, since the extra pace helps maintain distance control. It is common, so it will appear often.

Addon_Stalker_MirrorShard.name: Mirror Shard
Addon_Stalker_MirrorShard.description:
A large and sharp piece of a broken mirror.

Increases the base duration of Slaughtering Strike by 0.25 seconds.Decreases the charge speed of Slaughtering Strike by 25%.

beginner.whatItIs: An oversized shard of broken glass that extends the active duration of Slaughtering Strike. The recharge slows in exchange, so the killer must be more selective about when to swing.
beginner.whyItMatters: The longer active window gives a bigger moment to land the hit, which is more forgiving in tight spaces. The slower recharge means the killer cannot spam the strike, a small trade-off that favors patience over aggression.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer tends to miss Slaughtering Strike in close quarters, since the extra active time makes the timing more forgiving. It is a rare drop.

Addon_Stalker_ReflectiveFragment.name: Reflective Fragment
Addon_Stalker_ReflectiveFragment.description:
A tiny piece of a highly reflective material most probably from a broken mirror.

Hitting a Survivor with Slaughtering Strike adds 20 seconds to Evil Incarnate's duration.Slaughtering Strike only deals a single health state of damage.

beginner.whatItIs: An ultra-fine sliver of reflective material that lets a successful Slaughtering Strike hit extend Evil Incarnate. The strike is reduced to a single health state of damage in exchange.
beginner.whyItMatters: Trading raw damage for extended final-phase time is a bigger philosophical shift. The strike becomes a setup tool that prolongs the kill rather than an instant finisher, rewarding anyone who already lands these hits cleanly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer has high confidence in landing Slaughtering Strike and wants to stretch the final phase for more sustained pressure. It is very rare.

Addon_Stalker_ScratchedMirror.name: Scratched Mirror
Addon_Stalker_ScratchedMirror.description:
A standing portable vanity mirror which has been violently scratched with a sharp metallic object.

Reveal the auras of Survivors within 32 meters while stalking.Cannot leave Stalker Mode.Score events for hits grant 100% more Brutality and 200% more Deviousness Bloodpoints.

beginner.whatItIs: An iridescent vanity mirror, scratched with a sharp object, that reveals survivor auras at long range while stalking. The killer cannot leave Stalker Mode, and Score events for hits grant greatly boosted Brutality and Deviousness Bloodpoints.
beginner.whyItMatters: The aura reveal turns stalking into a long-range vision tool, but the inability to leave Stalker Mode is a heavy constraint. The killer must commit fully to the stalking phase for the entire trial, making this a bold and all-in choice.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants to hunt from a distance and does not mind being locked in the stalking phase for the whole trial. It is iridescent, the rarest tier here, so expect long waiting periods between pulls.

Addon_Stalker_TackyEarrings.name: Tacky Earrings
Addon_Stalker_TackyEarrings.description:
A very cheap piece of jewelry made from plastic. Painted to resemble precious material.

Increases movement speed while stalking by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Slots into Evil Within and adds a noticeable movement speed boost while in Stalker Mode. The effect is a steady, always-on speed increase rather than a burst or a timed window.
beginner.whyItMatters: The speed increase makes the stalking phase faster and more threatening. It closes the gap between a survivor's escape speed and the killer's pursuit, a small but steady quality bump that compounds over a full trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the map is large and open, since the extra pace helps keep up with fast-moving survivors across long stretches. It is common, so it will appear frequently.

Addon_Stalker_TombstonePiece.name: Tombstone Piece
Addon_Stalker_TombstonePiece.description:
A fist-sized granite piece taken from a broken tombstone.

When Evil Incarnate activates, you become Undetectable for 20 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Feeds into Evil Within and grants a brief window of Undetectable status the instant Evil Incarnate activates. The invisibility is a one-time burst at the start of the phase, not a persistent effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: That invisible window at the start of the final phase lets the killer reposition or set up a kill without being seen. It is a small but high-impact tool for turning the tables on survivors who try to predict the next move.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Fit it into a setup that leans on catching survivors who freeze during the late stage, since the brief undetectable window on activation scrambles their read on where you are. Because it is very rare, expect to wait before it lands.

Addon_Stalker_VanityMirror.name: Vanity Mirror
Addon_Stalker_VanityMirror.description:
A standing portable vanity mirror in perfect condition except for a fine layer of dust and face powder covering it.

When Evil Incarnate ends, you see the auras of all Survivors for 4 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Attaches to Evil Within and reveals all survivor auras for a short window the moment Evil Incarnate ends. The reveal is a single burst at the transition, not a continuous effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: That brief vision burst is a small but precise tool for finding survivors who scatter the instant the final phase drops. It closes information gaps that would otherwise let them hide in the open and break the chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the lobby tends to have survivors split up and go quiet at the end of Evil Incarnate, since the short reveal window helps track down the ones who slip away. It is very rare.

Addon_TheOnryo_01.name: Videotape Copy
Addon_TheOnryo_01.description:
A copy of the deadly videotape imprinted upon by Sadako. It dampens the desire for vengeance.

Increases the range at which Survivors gain Condemned from Projection by 2 meters

beginner.whatItIs: Deluge of Fear gets a wider Condemned radius from a videotape copy. Survivors gain Condemned from Projection at a greater distance, catching more of them in each activation.
beginner.whyItMatters: A wider Condemned radius means more survivors are affected by each Projection. The power becomes easier to use in group situations where targets are spread out rather than clustered in one spot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it in when the lobby scatters survivors across distant generators, since the widened Condemned reach from Projection pulls a larger share into the mark per cast. As a common drop it appears often enough to stay on your rotation.

Addon_TheOnryo_02.name: Old Newspaper
Addon_TheOnryo_02.description:
It tells of a local woman who predicted a volcanic eruption, evidence used to initially find Sadako.

Increases the Manifestation invisibility duration by 33%.

beginner.whatItIs: Deluge of Fear gains a longer Manifestation invisibility window from an old newspaper clipping. The invisible phase lasts noticeably longer, giving more time to reposition.
beginner.whyItMatters: Extending the Manifestation window hands the killer extra room to drift into position or re-aim the next play before the fog lifts. That is a modest quality lift, yet on a power that leans so hard on staying hidden even a brief stretch of cover changes how confidently a chase setup can land.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants to play more aggressively out of Manifestation and needs extra time to line up the next move. It is common and will show up with regularity.

Addon_TheOnryo_03.name: Cabin Sign
Addon_TheOnryo_03.description:
The cabin where both Tomoko and Reiko watched the tape. Carries the memory of those first curses.

Decreases the time it takes for a TV to turn on after Projection by 4.5 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Deluge of Fear activates TV projections faster after a cabin sign reduces the startup delay. The delay between Projection and the TV turning on is shorter, making the transition snappier.
beginner.whyItMatters: A shorter activation delay makes the projection feel less telegraphed. Survivors who use the pause to escape get less warning, which is a small but meaningful timing improvement.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the lobby has survivors who learn the activation rhythm and use the pause to escape, since the faster trigger closes that safety window. It is a common drop, expected to appear without long waits.

Addon_TheOnryo_04.name: Mother's Mirror
Addon_TheOnryo_04.description:
A mirror from Sadako's mother's house. A reminder of what Sadako has lost.

Increases the Manifestation intermittent visibility duration by 2 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: One common offering from Sadako's mother's house that extends the brief visible moments during Manifestation. The intermittent visibility windows last longer, making the killer easier to spot between invisible phases.
beginner.whyItMatters: Those slightly longer visible windows increase the risk of being tracked while in Manifestation. The trade-off suits a playstyle that leans on repositioning rather than pure stealth, since the killer is already moving with purpose.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer prefers to use Manifestation as a repositioning tool and does not mind being briefly visible, since the longer windows are less punishing when the killer is already in motion. It is common, so expect to see it without much patience.

Addon_TheOnryo_05.name: Reiko's Watch
Addon_TheOnryo_05.description:
The watch that Reiko left her son Yoichi. A distracting and constant reminder of one’s impending doom.

Increases the invisibility duration while Demanifested by 25%.

beginner.whatItIs: One uncommon watch left behind by Reiko that extends the invisibility duration while Demanifested. The hidden phase after a Manifestation lasts longer, giving more time to plan the next move.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer Demanifested window gives the killer more time to stay hidden after a Manifestation. It is a small but steady quality bump that makes the stealth cycle feel less pressured and more deliberate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it in lobbies where you want a slower, stealth-forward tempo and need the Demanifested state to hold a little longer while lining up the next projection. It lands at uncommon rarity, so the drop pool surfaces it more often than a very rare find.

Addon_TheOnryo_06.name: Sea-Soaked Cloth
Addon_TheOnryo_06.description:
The hood worn by the mysterious figure in the tape. Makes those near it unable to trust what they see.

While Survivors are within 8 meters of a powered TV, they are afflicted with the Blindness status effect. This effect lingers for 7 seconds after the TV is turned off.

Blindness prevents Survivors from seeing auras.

beginner.whatItIs: Slots into Deluge of Fear to blind survivors who linger near a powered TV, wiping out their aura vision. The blindness sticks around briefly after the screen goes dark, so the danger outlasts the instant the TV shuts down.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stripping aura vision in a TV zone denies survivors their primary way of spotting the killer or each other, which makes generators and windows near TVs far more dangerous to work on. The lingering effect after the TV is killed extends that pressure beyond the moment of shutdown.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in trials where survivors camp near TVs to hide or repair, since the lingering blindness after a TV goes dark still punishes anyone who lingers in the zone. It is an uncommon drop, so look for it before locking in a TV-control build.

Addon_TheOnryo_07.name: Clump of Hair
Addon_TheOnryo_07.description:
Once beautiful and long, Sadako now hides behind her ragged, matted locks.

Decreases the range at which The Onryō is visible while Demanifested by 6 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: Attaches to Deluge of Fear and narrows the distance from which survivors can spot The Onryo while she is Demanifested. The tighter window makes it harder for them to react the moment the manifestation ends and movement resumes.
beginner.whyItMatters: A shorter visible radius during demanifestation gives the killer a wider band of cover to close distance or reposition before survivors notice the shift. That extra concealment window is most valuable when The Onryo is actively hunting rather than setting up a manifest.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in matchups where The Onryo tends to be spotted too early during demanifestation, since the reduced visibility helps the killer slip into position. It is an uncommon drop and pairs well with any build that relies on closing distance quickly.

Addon_TheOnryo_08.name: Well Stone
Addon_TheOnryo_08.description:
A piece of the well where Sadako was trapped, an image burned into the mind of all those who have watched the tape.

Decreases the time it takes for a TV to turn on after being turned off by a Survivor by 7 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Plugs into Deluge of Fear and cuts the wait time before a switched-off TV powers back on. The shorter gap between shutdown and reactivation keeps the screen cycle tight, pressuring survivors to keep hunting for a fresh TV to turn off.
beginner.whyItMatters: A faster TV reset means survivors lose less time keeping a TV down, so the killer regains its TV-based effects more quickly. It matters most in trials where survivors prioritize cycling TVs to deny the killer's abilities.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when survivors are aggressively cycling TVs to shut down effects, since a quicker return to the on state keeps the killer's tools available between fights. As an uncommon drop it is an easy early pick for a TV-control build.

Addon_TheOnryo_09.name: Yoichi's Fishing Net
Addon_TheOnryo_09.description:
The net Yoichi used while fishing with his grandfather. A reminder that death comes to us all.

Survivors with at least 4 stacks of Condemned suffer from Blindness.

Blindness prevents Survivors from seeing auras.

beginner.whatItIs: Slots into Deluge of Fear and blinds survivors who have built up several Condemned stacks, stripping away their aura vision. The late-game effect can turn a long match into a scramble the moment the screen goes dark.
beginner.whyItMatters: The blindness hits hardest on survivors who have ignored the tape mechanic or kept lingering near TVs, compounding the curse pressure on exactly the survivors who most need their senses. It creates a clear escalation: the more a survivor engages with the curse, the less they can see.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that already generates Condemned stacks reliably, since the blindness only triggers once a survivor has collected enough of them. As an uncommon drop it fits naturally into a Condemned-focused kill flow.

Addon_TheOnryo_10.name: Rickety Pinwheel
Addon_TheOnryo_10.description:
A pinwheel found in the caves of Izu Oshima. It spins even when there is no wind, disorienting those who see or hear it.

While Survivors are within 8 meters of a powered TV, they are afflicted with the Oblivious status effect. This effect lingers for 7 seconds after the TV is turned off.

Oblivious prevents Survivors from hearing or being affected by the Killer's Terror Radius.

beginner.whatItIs: Replaces the Blindness effect near powered TVs in Deluge of Fear with Oblivious, which mutes survivors' ability to sense Terror Radius. The disorientation carries on briefly after the TV shuts off, so the killer's pressure zone stays hidden a little longer.
beginner.whyItMatters: Denying Terror Radius perception removes one of a survivor's key early warnings, opening room for The Onryo to reposition or approach without that tell. The lingering effect after a TV goes dark means survivors still lose that signal even after the immediate threat seems to have passed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants to close distance or flank without the terror radius giving away the approach, since the lingering Oblivious after a TV shutdown still blinds survivors to that cue. As a rare drop it rewards a build that commits to TV zone control.

Addon_TheOnryo_11.name: Well Water
Addon_TheOnryo_11.description:
Water from the well where Sadako was left to die. Murky and black, it obscures everything around it.

Increases the duration of the Undetectable status effect by 2 seconds when Manifesting by any means.

Undetectable hides the Killer's aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain.

beginner.whatItIs: Extends the Undetectable window The Onryo receives when manifesting under Deluge of Fear, keeping her aura, Terror Radius, and Red Stain hidden for longer. The extra invisibility gives more breathing room to set up the next move before survivors can read her position.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer invisible window after manifesting gives The Onryo more time to reposition, set up the next play, or slip away before survivors can track its aura, Terror Radius, or Red Stain. That extra cover matters most in the vulnerable moments right after a manifest.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in any build that relies on manifesting to set up the next chase, since the extra invisible time is exactly the window when The Onryo is most likely to be found. As a rare drop it suits a patient, repositioning-heavy kill style.

Addon_TheOnryo_12.name: Ring Drawing
Addon_TheOnryo_12.description:
A drawing of the view from inside the well, as drawn by a young Yoichi. Helping those cursed by the tape can only bring misfortune.

When hooking a Survivor carrying a tape, other Survivors gain 1 Condemned stack.

beginner.whatItIs: Ring Drawing changes what happens when The Onryo hooks a survivor who is carrying a tape: every other survivor in the trial also picks up a stack of Condemned at that moment. A single hook on the tape carrier ends up pushing the whole team's curse further along, not just one nearby person.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spreading Condemned to the group when the tape carrier is hooked punishes the whole team for failing to protect that survivor, and it accelerates the curse pressure on everyone at once. It turns a single hook into a team-wide setback.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when The Onryo wants to discourage teammates from clustering around the tape carrier, since hooking that survivor now costs the entire group an extra curse stack. As a rare drop it fits a build that already generates Condemned through other means.

Addon_TheOnryo_13.name: Bloody Fingernails
Addon_TheOnryo_13.description:
Sadako's bloody fingernails, lost as she tried to claw her way out of the well. Evidence of her single-minded need to kill.

Increases the duration of Projection’s bonus movement speed by 50%.

beginner.whatItIs: Bolts onto Deluge of Fear and stretches the movement speed bonus The Onryo enjoys while projected into a TV. The longer sprint window makes projecting to distant screens feel like a genuine map-travel tool rather than a short hop.
beginner.whyItMatters: A noticeably larger speed bonus during projection lets The Onryo cover more ground while possessing a TV, which makes long-distance repositioning through projection much more practical. It turns projection from a local effect into a cross-map tool.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when projection should double as a fast way to cross the map, since the stretched speed window turns a short hop into a proper reposition. It drops at a rare rate, so expect to wait a few chapters before it shows up, and pair it with a build that already leans on projecting to distant screens.

Addon_TheOnryo_14.name: Mother's Comb
Addon_TheOnryo_14.description:
The comb Sadako's mother used in the tape. Sadako's psychic abilities are enhanced when she focuses on it.

Turning off a TV will trigger a loud noise notification.Reveals the Aura of any TV that is turned off by any means.

beginner.whatItIs: Adds a loud noise and a visible aura reveal whenever a TV is switched off under Deluge of Fear, regardless of who or what caused the shutdown. The extra sensory cue lets The Onryo track which screens survivors have already visited and plan around the ones still active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Both the audible cue and the visible aura mark punish survivors for turning TVs off, since the action now announces itself to the killer and leaves a marker on the map. It discourages the usual TV-cycling counterplay that survivors use to deny the killer's effects.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it to deter survivors from aggressively cycling TVs, since every attempt to shut one off now gives The Onryo both a sound cue and a visible location marker. As a rare drop it suits a build that wants to control the TV counterplay.

Addon_TheOnryo_15.name: VCR
Addon_TheOnryo_15.description:
The original VCR that played Sadako's tape. It is still warm to the touch.

All TVs play the Projection effects when The Onryō Projects to a TV.

beginner.whatItIs: Overhauls Deluge of Fear so that every TV on the map carries the full Projection effects whenever The Onryo projects to any single screen. The global reach turns projection from a localized trick into a map-wide commitment, which reshapes how survivors plan their routes.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spreading the projection effect to all TVs at once multiplies the zone of influence the killer can control, turning a single projection into a map-wide tool. Survivors can no longer treat a far TV as a safe corner, since every screen is now an extension of the projected one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that wants maximum map control from a single projection, since every TV now acts as if it were the projected one. As a very rare drop it rewards a patient kill flow that builds around TV placement.

Addon_TheOnryo_16.name: Distorted Photo
Addon_TheOnryo_16.description:
Those who have watched the tape find all photos of them distorted, a reminder of their impending doom.

Survivors witnessing a Manifestation from within 16 meters will scream, and then their auras are shown for 4 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Turns Deluge of Fear's manifestations into a detection event, making survivors who witness one from a moderate distance scream and briefly reveal their auras. The exposed window hands The Onryo a clean target the instant a survivor peeks at the wrong screen.
beginner.whyItMatters: Forcing survivors to expose themselves in the moment they see the killer manifest gives The Onryo a clear window to chase or reposition, and the scream also alerts other survivors to the location. It punishes the habit of watching from the edge of a room rather than committing to a repair or escape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors tend to watch manifest from a safe distance, since their own auras light up in the exact moment they least expect it. At its very rare drop rate, plan around long gaps between pulls and let it feed into a build that converts each manifest into a chase opening.

Addon_TheOnryo_17.name: Telephone
Addon_TheOnryo_17.description:
After watching the video, victims receive a phone call. They are frozen in fear as they realize they have seven days to live.

Manifestation afflicts Survivors within 7 meters with a 3% Hindered status effect for 3 seconds.

Hindered reduces survivor movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Applies a brief movement slow to survivors caught near the manifestation point when Deluge of Fear fires. The Hindered effect is modest in strength but lands at the worst possible moment, right as a survivor is deciding whether to commit to a loop.
beginner.whyItMatters: Even a minor slow applied at the exact moment the killer appears can cost a survivor the gap needed to turn a corner or reach a pallet, making the first seconds of a chase harder to escape. It turns the moment of manifestation into a small but real chase disadvantage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it to make the instant of manifestation a slight but tangible escape penalty, since the brief slow hits hardest when a survivor is mid-sprint and trying to build distance. As a very rare drop it fits a build that relies on clean first-contact chases.

Addon_TheOnryo_18.name: Tape Editing Deck
Addon_TheOnryo_18.description:
The editing deck used by Reiko and Ryuji to analyze and copy the tape. Copying and sharing the tape is the only way to survive the curse.

Each Survivor starts the trial with a Tape in their possession, and their target TV is the furthest from their location.Anytime a Survivor inserts a tape in their target TV, reveal their aura for 6 seconds

beginner.whatItIs: Slots into Deluge of Fear on The Onryo, giving every survivor a tape at trial start and assigning each one the furthest TV as their target. Inserting the tape into that TV exposes the survivor's aura, so the power now forces survivors to reveal themselves to complete their side of the ritual.
beginner.whyItMatters: Forcing every survivor to carry and insert a tape creates a new decision every round, and the aura reveal on insertion gives The Onryo a clear window to punish anyone who completes the task in the open. It spreads map-wide pressure without requiring The Onryo to be nearby.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when The Onryo wants to force survivors into exposing themselves through their own ritual, because each one now holds a tape that will betray their position if inserted. Its very rare drop rate suits a patient kill flow that builds pressure before locking into a chase.

Addon_TheOnryo_19.name: Remote Control
Addon_TheOnryo_19.description:
A remote for the VCR at the cabin. It allows Sadako to focus on those enemies at a distance.

After using Projection, the Auras of Survivors who are within 12 meters of a powered TV are revealed to you for 7 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: A VCR remote that fits into Deluge of Fear on The Onryo, turning the Projection action into a scouting tool. Once the projection fires, survivors standing close to a powered TV have their auras briefly exposed.
beginner.whyItMatters: The post-projection aura reveal gives The Onryo a clear picture of where survivors are clustered around TVs, making follow-up chases or repositions much easier to set up. It converts the projection moment into an information play as well as a zone control tool.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when survivors tend to camp near TVs to deny effects, since the post-projection reveal is most valuable in exactly those situations. As an iridescent drop it is a high-investment pick for a build that commits fully to TV zone control.

Addon_TheOnryo_20.name: Iridescent Videotape
Addon_TheOnryo_20.description:
The original tape containing Sadako’s curse.

Projection does not turn off TVs, and does not apply Condemned.Increases the time it takes for a TV to turn on after being turned off by Survivors by 20%

beginner.whatItIs: Replaces the original curse tape for Deluge of Fear on The Onryo, so Projection no longer cuts power to TVs or marks survivors with Condemned. It also stretches the delay a TV needs before it can be switched back on after a survivor shuts it down.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the Condemned penalty and keeping TVs active shifts the power toward sustained zone control rather than curse accumulation, and the longer off-to-on delay punishes survivors who try to cycle TVs. It is a distinct shift in how the power plays, trading short-term curse pressure for long-term map control.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that prioritizes keeping TVs active over stacking Condemned, since the trade-off favors sustained zone control and denies survivors their usual TV-cycling counterplay. As an iridescent drop it is a statement pick for a TV-control kill flow.

Addon_Toolbox_001.name: Scraps
Addon_Toolbox_001.description:
Springs, screws and gears. Mostly unusable junk.

Adds 8 charges to the Toolbox.

beginner.whatItIs: A common toolbox add-on that packs extra repair charges into a survivor's kit. The added capacity lets a survivor fix more gear across a trial before the toolbox runs dry.
beginner.whyItMatters: More charges mean the toolbox stays available for longer stretches of the trial, which matters most when the killer is sabotaging hooks repeatedly. It is a straightforward way to make the toolbox last through a full match.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on any repair-focused survivor build, since the extra charges simply stretch how long the toolbox stays useful. As a common drop it is easy to find and pairs with any other toolbox add-on.

Addon_Toolbox_002.name: Wire Spool
Addon_Toolbox_002.description:
A portable but heavy spool of copper wire.

Adds 12 charges to the Toolbox.

beginner.whatItIs: An uncommon toolbox add-on made from a heavy spool of copper wire, adding a larger charge pool than the common scraps option. The extra capacity suits a survivor who plans to keep fixing gear throughout the whole trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: The bigger charge pool means the toolbox can sustain more hook repairs across a full trial, which is most valuable when the killer is sabotaging hooks aggressively throughout the match. It extends the window in which a survivor can keep hooks functional.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer is known to sabotage hooks frequently, since the extra charges keep the toolbox from running empty mid-trial. As an uncommon drop it is a solid step up from the common scraps option.

Addon_Toolbox_003.name: Clean Rag
Addon_Toolbox_003.description:
A mundane rag. Suspiciously clean.

Increases the Toolbox's repair speed by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Clean Rag speeds up how quickly a survivor's Toolbox repairs progress, so any job the toolbox is used on gets done in less time. It is a straightforward efficiency boost rather than something tied to any one specific task like hooks.
beginner.whyItMatters: Finishing a repair sooner means less total time spent committed to that action, which lowers the odds of getting caught mid-task if a killer closes in. It makes the Toolbox a more efficient tool across whatever job it gets used on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it whenever a build leans on the Toolbox as a go-to repair tool and wants every use of it to go a little faster. It suits a survivor who expects to spend a lot of time using the toolbox across a trial.

Addon_Toolbox_004.name: Grip Wrench
Addon_Toolbox_004.description:
An adjustable wrench with a tough grip. Essential in any Toolbox.

Hooks sabotaged using the Toolbox take an extra 20 seconds to respawn.

beginner.whatItIs: The Grip Wrench slots into the toolbox and extends how long a sabotaged hook stays down before it returns. That added gap gives a survivor room to reposition or work elsewhere instead of rushing back to the same hook under pressure.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer cooldown between hook sabotages gives the group more consistent access to hooks for rescues and resets, which disrupts the killer's ability to keep cycles short by re-sabotaging the same hooks. It is a quiet but meaningful counter to hook-heavy kill styles.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it onto a team that plans to break hooks near a chase to slow the killer down and protect a teammate, since the longer wait before a broken hook comes back makes each sabotage count for more. It rewards a group that already builds its rescues around denying hooks to the killer.

Addon_Toolbox_005.name: Hacksaw
Addon_Toolbox_005.description:
A small hand saw mounted with a metal cutting blade.

Increases the Toolbox's sabotage speed by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Mounted into the toolbox, the Hacksaw speeds up the hook-cutting action and shrinks how long someone stands exposed while working. The quicker finish helps most in tight spots where a long channel leaves the worker wide open to an incoming swing.
beginner.whyItMatters: A faster action means less time spent in the vulnerable commitment of working on a hook, which lowers the chance that the killer interrupts. It is most useful in situations where the toolbox is used under time pressure, such as during a chase or near a generator.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the toolbox's action needs to happen quickly under pressure, since the speed boost shortens the window in which the killer can interrupt. As a rare drop it suits a survivor who uses the toolbox frequently and wants to minimize exposure time.

Addon_Toolbox_006.name: Protective Gloves
Addon_Toolbox_006.description:
Thick gloves which reduce manual dexterity but protect hands from injury.

Prevents the Killer from being notified when sabotaging a hook with the Toolbox.

beginner.whatItIs: An add-on for the Toolbox that trades some manual dexterity for hand protection. The key mechanical change is that sabotaging a hook no longer sends a notification to the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing that ping is a bigger shift in hook play than a small tweak, because the killer loses the fastest cue for where a survivor was just dropped. Hooked survivors stay hidden until the killer happens to walk nearby.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when your role in the match is hook management and each drop needs to stay silent. At uncommon rarity it appears in item drops with regularity, so grab it whenever it shows up.

Addon_Toolbox_007.name: Brand New Part
Addon_Toolbox_007.description:
This intricate mechanical part feels oddly out of place. It is clean and shiny as if straight out of the factory.

Toolbox Repair action is replaced with Install Brand New Part.During the installation, you will be faced with a difficult Skill Check.Upon succeeding the Skill Check, the generator's required charges are reduced by 10.This add-on is consumed after use.

beginner.whatItIs: Swaps the standard Toolbox repair action for a Skill Check to install a brand-new part. A successful check reduces the generator's remaining charges, and the add-on is consumed on use.
beginner.whyItMatters: Turning a timed repair into a single high-stakes moment is a bigger shift, since it can close out a generator in one burst instead of a slow grind. The risk is that a failed check wastes the attempt and the item itself.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a generator is nearly done and the killer is far enough away that a missed check will not trigger a chase. It is iridescent, the rarest toolbox drop a survivor can find.

Addon_Toolbox_008.name: Instructions
Addon_Toolbox_008.description:
Someone quickly painted what seems to be repair instructions on this piece of bark.

Eliminates Skill Checks while repairing with the Toolbox.

beginner.whatItIs: Removes every Skill Check from Toolbox repairs outright. The repair action becomes a pure progress bar with no chance of a failed roll.
beginner.whyItMatters: Eliminating the Skill Check is a clean quality-of-life tweak that strips the failure risk from what is otherwise a tense action. A survivor can finish a generator under pressure without the stress of a random check.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it whenever the Toolbox is the repair tool of choice, since it removes the element that makes that action dangerous. At common rarity it is the easiest toolbox add-on to find in drops.

ADDON_toolbox_cuttingwire.name: Cutting Wire
ADDON_toolbox_cuttingwire.description:
A rudimentary cutting tool made from a jagged metal wire and two wooden handles.

Increases the Toolbox's sabotage speed by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Speeds up how quickly a Toolbox can sabotage a hook, letting a survivor disable it faster to stop a sacrifice. It is a straightforward boost to that one action with no other changes.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster sabotage means less time standing still at a hook, which lowers the window where a killer can interrupt or catch a survivor in the act. It matters most when racing to disable a hook before a sacrifice happens.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when sabotaging a hook quickly matters, especially in trials where the killer is camping and a fast disable can save a rescue. It is uncommon and will show up regularly.

ADDON_toolbox_socketswivels.name: Socket Swivels
ADDON_toolbox_socketswivels.description:
Swivels provide bend and flexibility for bolts that are out of reach, deep within mechanical devices.

Increases the Toolbox repair speed by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Uncommon in the pool, Socket Swivels increase Toolbox repair speed so each use adds more progress to a generator. It is a pure repair-speed boost with no trade-offs.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster repairs mean fewer Toolboxes needed to finish a generator, which keeps the item in inventory longer and reduces trips to loot chests. It is a steady improvement for any role centered on generator progress.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if the role centers on adding progress to generators and each Toolbox should do more work per swing. It is uncommon, so it will appear in the pool with reasonable frequency.

ADDON_toolbox_springclamp.name: Spring Clamp
ADDON_toolbox_springclamp.description:
Useful tool to clamp hoses or hold wires in place and prevent damage or injury.

The distance at which your repairs can be heard is reduced by 8 meters.

beginner.whatItIs: Spring Clamp quiets the sound of repair work, keeping the killer from hearing generator progress from as far away as before. It is an uncommon Toolbox add-on built around staying unheard while fixing generators.
beginner.whyItMatters: A smaller audible radius means a killer standing just outside the normal hearing range will no longer get tipped off by generator clicks. It is a meaningful shift for any survivor who wants to work unseen.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it in whenever the killer leans on listening to pin down a generator, because the quieter work keeps the position hidden for longer. As an uncommon drop it appears fairly often in the pool, so it is worth grabbing when it shows up in a listen-heavy match.

ADDON_TormentMode_BlackStrap.name: Black Strap
ADDON_TormentMode_BlackStrap.description: A nylon strap that was used to restrain a victim to a metal frame. The color makes it difficult to see the blood soaked into it.Decreases the range of Punishment of the Damned by 25%.Increases the width of Punishment of the Damned by 25%.

beginner.whatItIs: Plugs into Rites of Judgment, shortens the reach of Punishment of the Damned, and widens its beam. The result is a shorter but broader arc of damage hugging the ground closer.
beginner.whyItMatters: A tighter, wider beam covers more lateral space up close, which suits chokepoints and tight rooms where range is less important than catching someone off-angle. It reads as a small tactical tweak rather than a fundamental change to how the power plays.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when Punishment of the Damned falls short of distant survivors and the wider beam helps catch nearby ones in a tight room. It is common, so it is a reliable low-tier option.

ADDON_TormentMode_BurningManPainting.name: Burning Man Painting
ADDON_TormentMode_BurningManPainting.description: A diagram of the Lakeview Hotel. Red flames are painted over this place of guilt.When missing Punishment of the Damned, see the auras of Survivors within 3 meters for 6 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Sits in Rites of Judgment and reveals nearby survivor auras for a brief moment whenever a Punishment of the Damned shot falls wide. The miss stops being a pure waste and starts feeding information back to the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: A whiffed beam normally burns the cooldown for nothing, but the aura flash redirects the next swing toward a now-visible position. It softens the risk of missing and keeps momentum going between setups.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if Punishment of the Damned shots often miss and the follow-up information helps recover the wasted cooldown. It is rare, so it is not the hardest to find.

ADDON_TormentMode_CinderellaMusicBox.name: Cinderella Music Box
ADDON_TormentMode_CinderellaMusicBox.description: A music box with a figure from the fairy tale Cinderella. Found inside a suitcase adorned with stickers from multiple destinations.Decreases Punishment of the Damned's cooldown by 10%.

beginner.whatItIs: Attaches to Rites of Judgment and trims the cooldown on Punishment of the Damned, letting the beam come back a little sooner after each swing. The change is modest but compounds across a full match.
beginner.whyItMatters: Bringing the beam back faster matters most in rooms with multiple survivors, where a second shot is needed before the first fades. It reads as a small tuning nudge rather than a rework of the power's core loop.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the build wants to keep pressure on a generator room and one beam per cycle does not feel like enough. It is an uncommon find, so it should turn up somewhat regularly.

ADDON_TormentMode_CopperRing.name: Copper Ring
ADDON_TormentMode_CopperRing.description: Found in the basement of Brookhaven Hospital. It’s engraved with a picture of a spider.Increases maximum duration of Rites of Judgment by 5 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Slots into Rites of Judgment and stretches the maximum duration of the Rites state, buying extra time inside the setup window. The beam itself is unchanged; only the clock running against it ticks slower.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer window means trails can be laid more casually and a Punishment of the Damned line can be taken without rushing the swing. It reads as a comfort tweak that reduces the penalty for slow map setup.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the Rites window feels like it ends too quickly before a good beam setup is ready. It is a common find, so it is an easy grab for a casual build.

ADDON_TormentMode_CrimsonCeremoneyBook.name: Crimson Ceremony Book
ADDON_TormentMode_CrimsonCeremoneyBook.description:
A book about an ancient god. Author unknown.Survivors damaged by Punishment of the Damned suffer from the Hemorrhage and Mangled status effects for 80 seconds.

Hemorrhage regresses healing progress when not healing, and increases blood trails left by injured survivors. This lasts for a set duration or until healed.

Mangled increases time required to heal by 25% and lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Attaches to Rites of Judgment and tags any survivor struck by a beam with both Hemorrhage and Mangled. The two debuffs bleed healing progress and drag out repair time for a long stretch after the hit lands.
beginner.whyItMatters: One landed beam now carries two lingering penalties, so a single swing keeps taxing survivor recovery long after the chase ends. It reads as a heavy shift in how hard it is to heal once the beam connects.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when Punishment of the Damned shots land regularly and each hit should keep punishing healing at the generator. It is a very rare find, so treat it as a deliberate long-term pick.

ADDON_TormentMode_DeadButterfly.name: Dead Butterfly
ADDON_TormentMode_DeadButterfly.description: A butterfly found on a bed at Wood Side Apartments. It’s frail and nearly falls apart when touched.Increases Rites of Judgment's recharge rate by 10%.

beginner.whatItIs: Fits Rites of Judgment and speeds up how quickly the Rites state recharges, shrinking the idle gap between activations. The trails and the beam work exactly the same; only the wait between setups gets shorter.
beginner.whyItMatters: Less dead time between setups means the killer can keep re-engaging without a long cooldown stall. It reads as a tempo change that keeps pursuit mode active more often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the gap between Rites states feels too long and the killer ends up standing still waiting for it to return. It is common, so it is a low-effort quality-of-life pick.

ADDON_TormentMode_ForgottenVideotape.name: Forgotten Videotape
ADDON_TormentMode_ForgottenVideotape.description: A videotape of two lovers vacationing in Silent Hill. Despite its sentimental value, it was left behind in the Lakeview Hotel.Increases the speed at which Punishment of the Damned travels by 10%.

beginner.whatItIs: Plugs into Rites of Judgment and makes the Punishment of the Damned beam travel faster toward its target. The range and width stay the same; only the time it takes to cross the gap shrinks.
beginner.whyItMatters: A beam that arrives sooner gives survivors less time to sidestep or drop a pallet at the last instant. It reads as a small but meaningful edge in tight chases where reaction speed decides the hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors are consistently dodging the beam at the last second or standing just beyond the normal travel time. It is uncommon, so it is reasonably easy to find.

ADDON_TormentMode_IridescentSealofMetatr.name: Iridescent Seal of Metatron
ADDON_TormentMode_IridescentSealofMetatr.description: A talisman with an odd design inscribed on it. The Entity’s influence seems to have altered it.Decreases the range of Punishment of the Damned by 50%.Punishment of the Damned's range increases by creating Rites of Judgment trails, up to a maximum of 200%.This resets when Punishment of the Damned hits a Survivor.

beginner.whatItIs: Fits into Rites of Judgment and caps the opening range of Punishment of the Damned at a short distance, then lets each trail laid stretch that reach outward until it covers a very long arc. A successful hit on a survivor snaps the range back to its short starting point.
beginner.whyItMatters: The build-up rewards patient trail placement, because the longer the setup, the further the final beam can reach. It reads as a big shift in the power's identity, turning it from a fixed-range tool into a scaling reward for map control.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when comfortable laying long Rites trails before firing and the goal is to hit a survivor from far down a corridor. Its iridescent rarity means it should be treated as a dedicated build choice rather than a casual grab.

ADDON_TormentMode_LeadRing.name: Lead Ring
ADDON_TormentMode_LeadRing.description: Found in a refrigerator. It’s engraved with a disgusting, bloated face.Increases the range of Punishment of the Damned by 25%.Decreases the width of Punishment of the Damned by 25%.

beginner.whatItIs: Pairs with Rites of Judgment and swaps the beam width of Punishment of the Damned for extra distance, so the shot reaches further but covers less lateral ground. The narrower column rewards a steady centered aim over a wide sweeping pass.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer, thinner beam punishes survivors who hide behind walls at range, but it is harder to land on someone moving perpendicular to the shot. It reads as a small aim trade rather than a fundamental rework.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors are stretched along a wall or corridor and a standard-width beam overshoots the line. Its common rarity makes it a low-cost way to test a longer-range playstyle.

ADDON_TormentMode_LeopardPrintFabric.name: Leopard-Print Fabric
ADDON_TormentMode_LeopardPrintFabric.description: A shred of pink, leopard print fabric. It’s difficult to tell what it was used for.Decreases the duration of stuns by 15% while using Rites of Judgment.

beginner.whatItIs: A Rites of Judgment add-on that shortens the duration of stun effects on survivors. Stunned survivors shake free a little sooner, keeping the chase moving instead of stalling in place.
beginner.whyItMatters: Trimming stun duration is a modest adjustment that keeps chases flowing rather than locking survivors down for a long beat. It suits a pace that favors repeated contact over holding a single target in place for an extended window.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if the Rites build already has enough stun pressure elsewhere and the shorter stun duration is an acceptable trade. It is uncommon, so it is not hard to find.

ADDON_TormentMode_LostMemoriesBook.name: Lost Memories Book
ADDON_TormentMode_LostMemoriesBook.description:
A book about the history and legends of Silent Hill and the surrounding area.Survivors injured by Punishment of the Damned suffer from the Oblivious Status Effect for 80 seconds.

Oblivious prevents Survivors from hearing or being affected by the Killer's Terror Radius.

beginner.whatItIs: A Rites of Judgment add-on that tags injured survivors with the Oblivious status. While it lingers they lose all awareness of the killer's Terror Radius, removing the audio cue that normally warns them to flee.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stripping the audio warning for an extended stretch removes the one signal that prompts a survivor to bolt away from the hook, so they drift closer without realizing the danger is overhead. It is a meaningful shift in the loop around a hooked survivor, turning what would be an escape window into a blind spot the killer can exploit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the goal is dulling a survivor's sense of danger right after Punishment of the Damned lands. It is scarce in the add-on pool, so save it for a loadout built entirely around Rites of Judgment.

ADDON_TormentMode_MannequinFoot.name: Mannequin Foot
ADDON_TormentMode_MannequinFoot.description: The smooth grey foot of a mannequin, brutally torn from its leg.Rites of Judgment trails inflict Exhausted for 10 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: A Rites of Judgment add-on that makes the trail line apply the Exhausted status to any survivor who crosses through it. Cutting across the trail zone now carries a brief speed penalty on top of the beam risk.
beginner.whyItMatters: Adding Exhausted to trail contact changes how survivors route around the beam line, because the fastest escape path now costs them sprint speed. It reads as a small but sharp tweak that makes the trail zone feel like a hazard to cross rather than just a damage line to dodge.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when long Rites trails are already part of the plan and survivors should think twice before sprinting through them. It is a rare find, so it counts as a solid mid-tier option.

ADDON_TormentMode_MistyDayRemainsofJudgm.name: Misty Day, Remains of Judgment
ADDON_TormentMode_MistyDayRemainsofJudgm.description: A painting of an imposing figure wearing a steel pyramid atop his head. Victims are caged in the background.Injuring a Survivor with Punishment of the Damned reveals their aura for 8 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Slots into Rites of Judgment and briefly exposes a survivor's aura the instant a Punishment of the Damned hit connects. The short window rewards landing the beam mid-chase, when keeping visual contact matters most.
beginner.whyItMatters: A brief aura reveal after the beam hits lets the killer confirm the survivor's position and adjust the next attack toward where they are heading rather than guessing. It is a small but reliable tool for keeping pressure on a target that tries to slip away in the fog.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Reach for it in matches where beam hits land but a fleeing survivor tends to vanish into dark corners of the map. Since it shows up occasionally in the pool, count on it as a steady choice for staying on a target's heels.

ADDON_TormentMode_ObsidianGoblet.name: Obsidian Goblet
ADDON_TormentMode_ObsidianGoblet.description: An ancient looking goblet carved from pure obsidian.You can special-break Pallets and Breakable walls with Punishment of the Damned.Increases Punishment of the Damned's cooldown by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Goes onto Rites of Judgment and lets a Punishment of the Damned hit shatter pallets and breakable walls in place. The trade is a longer wait between activations, so timing each beam strike matters more than usual.
beginner.whyItMatters: Turning the beam into an obstacle-clearing tool opens up chases that would normally stall behind a pallet or a breakable wall. The extended cooldown, however, means each activation is a bigger commitment, so the power rewards picking the right moment to spend it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when chases keep dying behind pallets or breakable walls and the beam needs to punch through that cover. Because it is iridescent, treat it as a deliberate pick for a build that leans on clearing obstacles mid-chase.

ADDON_TormentMode_RustcoloredEgg.name: Rust-colored Egg
ADDON_TormentMode_RustcoloredEgg.description: An old-looking egg, colored reddish orange. About the size of a quail’s egg.Injuring a Survivor with Punishment of the Damned increases Rites of Judgment's charge by 30%.

beginner.whatItIs: Tethers to Rites of Judgment and feeds a chunk of the charge pool back whenever a Punishment of the Damned hit connects with a survivor. Each successful beam strike keeps the activation meter climbing, so sustained pressure during a hunt pays off.
beginner.whyItMatters: Feeding charge back into the pool on every landed hit tightens the loop between beam setups and Rites activations. It reads as a meaningful shift for sustained pressure, since the idle gap between uses shrinks noticeably.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a tight cycle between beam activations matters and a survivor is likely to stay in range for repeated hits. Its very rare slot means it is a commitment to a dedicated Rites build rather than a casual addition.

ADDON_TormentMode_ScarletEgg.name: Scarlet Egg
ADDON_TormentMode_ScarletEgg.description: A fresh egg, strikingly red in color. About the size of a quail’s egg.Survivors afflicted with Torment spawn Rites of Judgment trails when sprinting. These trails last 5 seconds.You no longer see the auras of Rites of Judgment trails.

beginner.whatItIs: Hooks into Rites of Judgment and makes Tormented survivors leave visible trails behind them while they sprint. It also hides the aura markers on those trails, so following a Tormented survivor's path depends on recall and what remains visible.
beginner.whyItMatters: Survivors who carry the Torment tag now leave a visible path as they flee, which can set up beam opportunities for the killer. On the flip side, losing the aura markers on those trails means the killer is working from memory and partial sight, turning the chase into a less predictable cat-and-mouse game.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Reach for it against groups that keep Torment stacked and sprint across open ground to escape. Its scarcity in the pool makes it a niche pick reserved for a build leaning hard into Rites of Judgment trail reads.

ADDON_TormentMode_Spearhead.name: Spearhead
ADDON_TormentMode_Spearhead.description: The sharp, rusted tip of a spear. It’s flaked with blood from its last victim.When a Survivor is saved from a Cage of Atonement, you see their rescuer's aura for 8 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Locks onto Rites of Judgment and briefly reveals the rescuer's aura the moment a survivor is pulled off a Cage of Atonement. The window is short, but it names who made the save, which is enough to adjust where the next pressure lands.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing which survivor rushed the save turns the hook area into a potential trap for the rescuer. It is a small but sharp deterrent that makes the save attempt riskier, since the killer now has a clear target to chase immediately after.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when saves should feel riskier, exposing the rescuer the moment they reach the cage. Because it is uncommon, it is an easy find in the pool and works as a reliable pick for a save-punishment setup.

ADDON_TormentMode_TabletoftheOppressor.name: Tablet of the Oppressor
ADDON_TormentMode_TabletoftheOppressor.description: A metal tablet engraved with Aztec figures.While using Rites of Judgment, gain the Undetectable Status Effect.

beginner.whatItIs: The Tablet of the Oppressor slots into Rites of Judgment and makes the killer undetectable while the ritual is in progress. It removes the aura entirely during the setup phase.
beginner.whyItMatters: Hiding your aura during the ritual removes the main way survivors notice and rush to interrupt, so the power plays much more smoothly once a spot is committed. It reads as a bigger shift in how Rites of Judgment functions rather than a small stat bump.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in matches where survivors keep breaking the ritual from across the map before it completes. It is a rare drop, so plan around it only when it shows up in the pool.

ADDON_TormentMode_ValtielSectPhotograph.name: Valtiel Sect Photograph
ADDON_TormentMode_ValtielSectPhotograph.description: A photograph of two figures in red hoods. Entitled Crimson and White Banquet for the Gods.Decreases your Terror Radius by 2 meters for each Survivor affected by Torment.

beginner.whatItIs: A rare add-on for Rites of Judgment that shrinks your Terror Radius each time a survivor is caught inside the Torment zone. The effect stacks as more survivors are judged.
beginner.whyItMatters: A smaller terror radius means fewer early warnings for anyone nearby, which compounds as the ritual catches more survivors and makes a whole generator area feel safe to work in. It reads as a meaningful control shift rather than a minor tweak.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when Rites of Judgment is being used as a map-control tool and the ritual should quietly reshape the area rather than just dealing damage. Its rare rarity means it will not be in every loadout.

ADDON_TormentMode_WaxDoll.name: Wax Doll
ADDON_TormentMode_WaxDoll.description: A doll carved from wax, handcrafted by a prisoner who would soon face their judgment.Increases the range of Punishment of the Damned by 5%.

beginner.whatItIs: Uncommon in rarity, the Wax Doll widens the range of Punishment of the Damned. It gives the damage phase of Rites of Judgment a slightly larger reach.
beginner.whyItMatters: A larger reach on the damage phase gives more room to finish off a survivor who stumbles into the edge of the zone. It turns a near-miss into a confirmed injury, which matters in close calls.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if survivors keep escaping the ritual damage by a small margin. It is uncommon, so it will rotate in and out of the pool between matches.

ADDON_trap_BloodyCoil.name: Bloody Coil
ADDON_trap_BloodyCoil.description:
Part sticky, part slippery, this grim liquid makes handling the traps' springs more dangerous.

When a Bear Trap is disarmed by a healthy Survivor, the bloody coils exact their price and that Survivor becomes injured.

beginner.whatItIs: Iridescent and punishing, Bloody Coil turns a healthy survivor's trap disarm into a guaranteed injury. It slots into Bear Trap and changes the outcome of a safe pop.
beginner.whyItMatters: Making a disarm hurt adds real teeth to the trap as a defensive tool, since even a survivor who knows they are stepping in it will come away injured. It reads as a bigger shift in Bear Trap deterrent value rather than a minor tweak.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when Bear Traps should discourage disarming rather than just catching, especially against survivors who have learned to pop them safely. Its iridescent rarity makes it a standout find when it appears.

ADDON_trap_DiamondStone.name: Iridescent Stone
ADDON_trap_DiamondStone.description:
Traps sharpened with this sickly gleaming stone seem to gain a life of their own.

Every 30 seconds, one closed Bear Trap chosen at random becomes set.

beginner.whatItIs: Very rare, the Iridescent Stone automatically sets a random closed Bear Trap at regular intervals. It removes the need to stand over traps waiting for the right moment.
beginner.whyItMatters: Self-setting traps spread map control across a wider area with less active management, which pairs well with a killer who wants to cover more ground. It is a bigger shift in how Bear Trap is played compared to a simple stat change.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a passive trap network should keep catching survivors while the killer is elsewhere on the map. It is an iridescent drop, so treat it as a rare and valuable find.

ADDON_trap_OilyCoil.name: Oily Coil
ADDON_trap_OilyCoil.description:
An oiled spring that marks the hands of those who meddle with a Bear Trap.

When resetting a Bear Trap, reveal the aura of the most recent Survivor to disarm it for 5 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: Rare and informative, Oily Coil reveals the aura of the survivor who most recently disarmed a trap for a short window when the trap is reset. It slots into Bear Trap and adds a tracking element.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing exactly where the disarming survivor is gives a chance to close the gap and re-engage, turning a wasted trap into a fresh chase opportunity. It reads as a meaningful information gain rather than a damage change.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors have figured out how to defuse Bear Traps and vanish before a chase can start, since the brief aura reveal on reset closes that escape window. It is very rare in the item pool, so treat it as a windfall and equip it the moment it appears.

ADDON_trap_RustedJaw.name: Rusted Jaws
ADDON_trap_RustedJaw.description:
These Bear Trap jaws are covered with crusty and volatile rust spots that makes injuries particularly difficult to heal.

Bear Traps inflict Mangled on trapped survivors for 70 seconds.

Mangled increases time required to heal by 25% and lasts for a set duration or until fully healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Rusted Jaws apply the Mangled condition to survivors caught in a Bear Trap, making subsequent healing take longer. It is a rare add-on that extends the punishment beyond the initial hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: A mangled survivor who is also injured has a much harder time patching up before the next chase arrives. It extends the vulnerability window well past the trap itself, which compounds with any other injury already on the survivor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a Bear Trap catch should carry the sting well beyond the chase, because the Mangled effect drags out every subsequent healing action for the trapped survivor. It lands in the pool as a rare drop, so stock it whenever one surfaces in a match where traps are already doing heavy lifting.

ADDON_trap_StitchedBag.name: Tension Spring
ADDON_trap_StitchedBag.description:
A high tension spring that snaps back into place after being stretched.

A Bear Trap resets 2 seconds after a Survivor escapes from it.

beginner.whatItIs: Slots into Bear Trap and makes the trap snap back to an armed state almost the instant a trapped survivor escapes. The shortened reset window means the same trap can catch again much sooner than usual.
beginner.whyItMatters: A trap that recovers faster keeps pressure on a team that keeps running through the same corridor, because the second catch arrives before survivors can adjust their route. It shifts the trap from a one-time hazard into a persistent threat on well-traveled paths.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when controlling a tight loop matters more than covering wide open ground, since the faster reset lets a single trap fire repeatedly. The drop is very rare, so expect long stretches of trials before it lands in the locker.

ADDON_trap_TrapSetters.name: Coffee Grounds
ADDON_trap_TrapSetters.description:
An old rusted can containing damp coffee grounds.

Increases the Haste status effect gained after setting a  Bear Trap by 5%.

Haste increases Killer movement speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Fits into Bear Trap and gives The Trapper a slight speed increase each time a new trap is placed. The boost is modest but steady, nudging overall pace upward with every placement during a trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra speed is a small mechanical tweak rather than a playstyle overhaul, but across a full trial it helps The Trapper reach the next trap spot faster and close gaps during chases. It rewards a killer who keeps moving and setting rather than standing still.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if you want The Trapper to feel a little quicker between placements, especially on large maps where covering ground between generators matters. It drops at an uncommon rate, so it should show up in your locker fairly often.

Addon_Trickster_01.name: Memento Blades
Addon_Trickster_01.description:
Blood-rusted knives, worn from overuse. Employed during Ji-woon's early murders, they hold a place of importance in his heart.

Displays a reticle while aiming with Blades.

beginner.whatItIs: Attaches to Showstopper, adding a visible reticle while aiming with Blades. The reticle helps line up throws at moving survivors.
beginner.whyItMatters: A visual aiming aid is a small but practical tweak that reduces the guesswork in every Blade throw. It makes it easier to land hits on targets that would otherwise require leading the shot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when learning The Trickster or when Blade accuracy feels inconsistent, since the extra visual aid smooths out the aiming process. At common rarity it is readily available from item drops.

Addon_Trickster_02.name: Trick Pouch
Addon_Trickster_02.description:
A pouch with a number of hidden pockets. Used by aspiring magicians and those with something to hide.

Increases maximum carried Blades by 8.Start the Trial with 8 additional Blades.

beginner.whatItIs: Raises the maximum Blade carry for Showstopper and starts the trial with extra Blades already in hand. More ammunition means more chances to land hits and build Style Ranks before a reload is needed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Carrying more Blades is a bigger shift in resource management, since it extends how long the killer can pressure a loop without returning to a locker. It also softens the early trial before the first reload opportunity arrives.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing a Blade-heavy build that relies on sustained pressure rather than isolated big hits. At common rarity it is a dependable drop that fits naturally into most Trickster kits.

Addon_Trickster_03.name: Killing Part Chords
Addon_Trickster_03.description:
A set of chords that Ji-woon never found a song for. Still, the sound is undeniably catchy.

Increases time before Style Ranks from D to A decay by 50%.

beginner.whatItIs: Slows the decay of Style Ranks between D and A by half for Showstopper. Higher ranks linger longer, giving more room to keep the combo alive.
beginner.whyItMatters: A wider decay window is a meaningful shift in how the rank system feels in practice, because the killer has more time to chain actions that maintain the current rank. It makes the rhythm of building and holding ranks less punishing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when building around sustained Style Rank pressure, since the longer window rewards a steady pace of Blade hits and environmental interactions. At common rarity it is a reliable drop to pick up.

Addon_Trickster_04.name: Inferno Wires
Addon_Trickster_04.description:
Burnt wires from the studio fire that killed four of the five NO SPIN members. Their deaths gave rise to The Trickster.

Increases the Style Rank timer of S-Rank by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: Extends the S-Rank timer for Showstopper so the top rank lingers longer. The extra time widens the window where all S-Rank bonuses are active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Lengthening the top-rank timer is a focused tweak that matters most when a kill setup is already in motion. More time at S-Rank means more room to land the finishing Blade without dropping the chain.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a kill is close and the goal is to hold S-Rank long enough to convert pressure into a down. At common rarity it is easy to find and pairs well with any Style Rank build.

Addon_Trickster_05.name: Ji-woon's Autograph
Addon_Trickster_05.description:
A signature from the celebrity known as The Trickster. Sore as his wrist was after hundreds of these, it was invigorating to know he was so in demand.

Increases the duration of Main Event by 44%.

beginner.whatItIs: Lengthens Main Event for Showstopper, buying more time in that empowered state. Every second of extra Main Event is extra time to pressure the remaining survivors.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer Main Event is a meaningful shift in the endgame, since it extends the window where the killer has a real advantage over all survivors at once. It turns a brief spike into a sustained pressure phase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when running a build that triggers Main Event and wants to stretch the payoff as far as possible. At uncommon rarity it is a solid drop to grab when it appears.

Addon_Trickster_06.name: On Target Single
Addon_Trickster_06.description:
An underground single produced by Ji-woon before achieving fame. Only the biggest NO SPIN fans collected this hidden gem.

Increases the duration of Main Event by 0.5 seconds for each Blade hit while in S-Rank, up to a maximum of 20 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: A rare Showstopper add-on that stacks Main Event duration with every Blade hit landed while in S-Rank. The more hits, the longer Main Event lasts once it triggers.
beginner.whyItMatters: Scaling Main Event with Blade hits is a bigger shift than a flat duration bump, because it rewards the killer for actually landing throws during the top rank. It turns S-Rank into a setup phase for an even longer Main Event.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a build already prioritizes S-Rank and the goal is to stretch Main Event into a long pressure window. At rare rarity it is a less common drop, so save it for matches where Main Event timing is the deciding factor.

Addon_Trickster_07.name: Lucky Blade
Addon_Trickster_07.description:
The first throwing knife Ji-woon ever owned. Purchased by his father, he was expected to put on a show for those frequenting the family restaurant.


On every eighth Blade Hit, an additional bonus is assigned at random:

Increases Throw Speed by 5% for 5 seconds.Gain 3% Haste for 6 seconds.Gain an additional Style Point.
